texts: youre killing communities ccp ccp your constant ignorance of the ingame economy has led to blunder after blunder heres an example miners are important to the eve online community they are also important to the microcommunities of lowsec wh space and every other space miners arent just targets to be ganked they are people living locally often successfully avoiding ganks which are exposed and tempted to join pvp activities by making mining activities nearly worthless in these areas it chases away these valuable community members the pool of potential pvpers in this game designed for pvp is lessened this leads to a gradual shrinking of pvpers to interact with do pvpers want to gank miners i mean if they are sitting there oblivious yeah theyll do it but is that really the challenge they are looking for no pvpers just want more people to have fun fights with that only happens when other community members get tempted to try pvp and voluntarily do it so how do we do that well first you have to get someone to move to an area with pvp by tempting them with better rewards this is where ccp is horribly horrendously failing at their job and the community knows it wh space is getting the worst of it not only have they recently received no changes but changes to other areas of space have lowered prices this lowers the rewards they get in much higher risk areas for example new wh space explorers often consisted of relic sites hunters looking for t2 salvage however now nullsec can spawn as many of these sites as they want so prices crashed massively now the relic sites have much lower rewards these new community members arent tempted to enter wh space lowsec also isnt getting the attention it deserves the introduction of new mining sites barely changed the volume of ore mined in lowsec thats because the risk vs reward for mining in lowsec had been so poor already that these laughable improvements dont change much ccp has clearly chosen to spread the items players need throughout the universe so that with some exceptions no one area exclusively controls the market and manufacturers can locally source as much as possible that could be ok if ccp balances resource distribution correctly they would have to take extreme care when buffing one area to buff all other areas this induces significant dev effort every time a minor change is made from our perspective this would look like less new content less often because this takes so much dev time obviously ccp doesnt do this they dont even understand that this is a macroeconomics situation they are playing with here buffs to one area when it shares a common resource with another area nerfs all other areas so what are we left with ccp continues to lazily and ignorantly change rewards to select areas which result in nerfs to other areas this results in the gradual shrinking of communities in those areas good fucking job

feedback on a story i am writing word count 4983 hello i am new to this subreddit ive been cooking up a story idea for about a year now and have finally decided to make it a reality im making more specifically a comic but i want some help with the story currently i have the main outline but i want some critiques on it ive never put my work out anywhere online before so im a bit nervous but you know i guess i need to get used to this aha note that this is more notes on how to tackle the story for me but again i just want to know if its actually a good story heres a background of the world this is set in in 2027 world war breaks out for a third time and its effects are devastating it lasts for around 5 years before ending with an event that kills three quarters of the world population the event was like a nuclear strike on steroids the story takes place in 2035 3 years after the war has ended the war caused earths climate to become practically unliveable and so a program was launched by a company that specialises in space travel three trained professionals a pilot a scientist and a mechanic are selected to be sent into space to explore and determine whether certain planets are either habitable or can help with restoring earths climate using resources a year into the program however things are paused when the mechanic of the mission goes missing and cannot be found a replacement is put on board our main character and our story begins there act one the story opens with a past recorded video of oliver the scientist ivan the missing mechanic and ana the pilot celebrating ivans birthday aboard the spaceship the footage is warm and playful but ends on an unsettling note when ivans smile falters as he looks past the camera held by ana before the recording abruptly cuts this moment plants early unease and foreshadows later revelations the scene transitions to emily in the present visually mirroring ivans physical position as she eats a meal at a table in a home setting emilys daily life is marked by emotional distance and quiet suffocation at home she is physically present but disengaged surrounded by her mother and younger brother yet unable to connect meaningfully with them news reports about worsening climate conditions play in the background largely ignored her mothers interactions with her are transactional focused on responsibility rather than conversation reinforcing emilys sense of being trapped after an argument breaks out with emilys brother and her mother her mother asks emily to walk her brother to school emily takes her brother to school and then commutes to work passing a protest outside a store selling oxygen masks a necessity in todays society due to the worsening climate during the confrontation she overhears people discussing ivan credited as one of the minds behind the technology whom emily believes is still part of the space mission the protestors openly criticize the company responsible for the program doing space travel as ivan is directly associated with them saying that its taking too long and such emily walks away only for it to be revealed that she herself works for that same company at work emily is shown to be highly capable and quietly indispensable she manufactures requested machinery fixes equipment for coworkers and operates under poor conditions without complaint when a serious accident nearly kills a colleague due to faulty wiring emily intervenes and saves them using her expertise despite being praised she reacts with visible distress brushing off attention rather than accepting it immediately after emily is summoned by her boss and informed of a hiccup in the space program a crewmate is missing and the company is desperate for a replacement emily is asked to be said replacement while they try to find ivan the request is framed less as an honor and more as a necessity it is also revealed here that emily applied for this job a year ago but got rejected in favour of ivan after being deemed mentally unstable after a work incident however is being picked now since she is the only one qualified enough for the position after brief hesitation she agrees that evening emily informs her family her mother and brother react poorly leading to an argument her mother doesnt want her to leave since emily is the main source of income for the family but also the main caretaker emily who does really want the job for her own selfish desires pursues the job regardless while she does feel a sense of responsibility for her family she wants to also take this job seeing it as an escape out of both her family life and earths horrible climate after a short time skip emily travels to the united states for the programs launch though her relationship with her mother remains unresolved she is given a tour of the facility and the spaceship itself she meets oliver who immediately attempts to put her at ease they get along though his enthusiasm contrasts with her restraint notably she does not yet meet ana that evening she attends a public relations event announcing the programs continuation following ivans disappearance emily is uneasy but supported by olivers presence ana and the programs director are present but not formally introduced emily delivers a speech that is awkward yet sincere managing to hold her ground despite visible protests afterward she retreats to a hallway to calm herself and briefly encounters a woman who makes an offhand comment about her new position asking her if its what she really wants the interaction is brief but its directness leaves emily confused on launch day emily is formally introduced to the crewoliver the director and ana who is revealed to be the same woman from the hallway emily is immediately uncomfortable but unable to withdraw before boarding she checks her phone and receives a short but reassuring message from her mother showing that while things are still unresolved between them there is still care act one ends with emily boarding the spaceship uncertain displaced but determined act two takes place several weeks after launch the act opens aboard the spaceship with emily repairing a malfunction in the cockpit ana observes closely marking items off a checklist as emily explains the problem and her solution oliver enters midtask having a cheery demeanour before mentioning that they are approaching their first target planet before landing ana briefs the crew on the planet and stresses strict adherence to protocol emily has no issue following orders but is still weary around ana while oliver appears uneasy with anas tone upon arrival they discover the planet is a barren wasteland contradicting the data ana was given evidence of a massive asteroid impact suggests a longpast mass extinction oliver questions the value of staying noting there is nothing viable for him to sample ana hesitates torn between mission expectations and the evidence in front of her without permission emily ventures ahead and discovers a network of underground caves although this leads the team to continue the mission ana grows noticeably colder toward emily for defying her authority as they explore emily proves her skill modifying equipment on the fly however she slips up at moments as well too eager to explore areas that ana has to prevent her from going to since they are dangerous despite this oliver becomes increasingly impressed and engages more openly with emily while anas frustration mounts after 3 days of searching with no tangible results ana orders a withdrawal emily argues to continue believing she is close to something meaningful but ultimately concedes that anas reasoning is sound they havent found a thing they return to the ship and set course for a second planet in the same system the first planets trip is rather short in comparison to the rest of the storys events later oliver reassures emily that her work mattered and admits that under different circumstances they might have found something significant during this conversation he reveals that ana is the directors daughter that night while on watch duty emily reviews mission logs from the first planet unsettled by a lingering feeling that something was missed while reorganizing nearby equipment she discovers old photographs and recordings of ivan oliver and ana after hesitating she watches one of the tapes a seemingly harmless moment between the three ana enters midviewing and reacts with disproportionate anger emily apologizes which calms ana down but its obvious that the mention of ivan struck a nerve for her emily awkwardly goes back to her station the next day the crew then arrives at the second planet which contrasts sharply with the firstlush vibrant and teeming with plant life the planet is marked uninhabitable due to a weak atmosphere despite its abundance of plants they determine the flora would not survive earths conditions due to how it can only survive in extremities ana is more irritable than before distancing herself from both emily and oliver oliver increasingly anxious stays close to emily and the two talk as they explore oliver shares fragments of his past during the war though he avoids emotional depth his past hints at his tendency of avoidance as his silence caused the deaths of many around him during the war including his family he was basically blackmailed into keeping quiet about government secrets but when he tried to tell people about it his family was killed so hes learnt that silence is survival they soon discover an abandoned human research base ana recognizes it but offers no explanation oliver tells emily that the planet had been studied during the war before being abandoned and that theyre back here to see if there were any unused research or samples that can be used but he doesnt elaborate further inside the base they uncover data suggesting that a rare plant species on one of the planets moons couldat least in theoryaid in restoring earths ecosystems for the first time the team shares a sense of genuine hope and agrees to investigate on the moon they find only a small patch of the plant growing in an extremely hazardous area emily proposes a plan that would safely retrieve the sample but at the cost of valuable resources ana rejects it in favor of a faster riskier approach the argument escalates and emily confronts ana personally bringing up ivan and questioning her judgment oliver remains silent shocked by emilys defiance ana now angered at emilys personal attack proceeds with her plan regardless however midway through it begins to fail causing emily to break away and execute her own plan despite oliver and ana shouting for her to stop fully aware she may die emily presses on framing the risk as both a chance to atone for her past elaborated later and to help save earth she nearly falls to her death but at the last moment ana intervenes pulling her to safety ana is visibly shaken her controlled exterior briefly cracking she says nothing the retrieved sample is damaged but oliver confirms it may still be salvageable with time the act ends with the crew returning to the ship in silence emily watches ana closely beginning to question whether her initial judgment of her was wrong meanwhile the room that emily found the tapes in has a light flashing next to one of the crewmates names a distress signal from ivan which has been going on for months act three opens with a flashback a young girl stands in a hospital corridor with her father doctors speak quietly to him while the girl stares through a window at a room where a woman lies motionless beneath a sheet her expression is eerily blank the father his face never shown explains that the woman is dead that she was the girls mother the child does not respond on the drive home the father tells her gently but firmly that they cannot dwell on this that they must move on and not talk about it again his voice betrays his grief even as he avoids it the girl remains silent only the slightest welling of her eyes suggests feeling beneath the surface the audience does not yet know who she is the story cuts back to the present aboard the ship several days have passed oliver and ana examine the salvaged plant sample but oliver has made little progress and is growing frustrated a restrained argument breaks out between them touching on unresolved tensions from their shared past before emily enters when she asks about the sample oliver dismisses her concern emily instead raises a practical issue one of the ships engines requires maintenance that will take several days and would be safer to complete on a planet ana considers their options and proposes a detour to a nearby planet she and oliver have visited beforestable resourcerich and suitable for both repairs and olivers research suggesting that resources there could even help with the sample emily hesitates about deviating from the plan but ana waves it off surprising her with a rare flexibility emily softens further toward ana while oliver is visibly relieved by the lack of conflict they land on the planet which is strikingly earthlike the atmosphere is breathable the landscape lush and calm emily asks why this planet was never seriously considered as a solution for earth ana explains that the planets seasons last for years with winters and summers so extreme they are lethal they have arrived during a brief deceptive autumn before winter sets in over the following days emily focuses on repairing the ship ana has to give her access control of the ship this is important while ana and oliver gather resources for the sample during downtime emily and oliver explore the planet together laughing and enjoying its beauty ana watches from a distance still reserved but no as cold she treats emily less like a subordinate and more like a teammate during one outing ana discovers something she missed on previous visits and becomes convinced there may be microbial life beyond plant matter emily volunteers to accompany her partly out of curiosity and partly because she is growing increasingly fascinated by ana herself as they search their conversation begins professionally but when emily thanks ana for saving her life weeks earlier something shifts ana initially deflects keeping it formal but eventually opens up as they walk the two exchange fragments of their pasts ana speaks about her strained relationship with her father shaped by emotional distance and unspoken loss this hints that anas desire involves a theme of denial about her situation emily in turn shares her experiences with workplace trauma and her complicated relationship with her mother revealing that during the war she left a coworker to die during an attack on their base this hints at emilys martyr complex how she pushes to help others so much because she feels immense guilt for leaving her coworker behind neither fully unpack their pain but there is recognition and understanding between them it is during this quiet bond that the audience realizes the girl in the opening flashback was ana they discover evidence of lifebacterial not sentientbut still significant the moment feels hopeful with ana collecting samples of the bacteria and saying its worth studying they return to the ship changed more aligned than before while ana and emily were exploring oliver briefly noticed something troubling in the ships systems a faint distress signal bearing ivans identifier he expertly disables the signal implying hes done it before but it doesnt shut off turning from orange to red panicked he covers it over with a blanket and leaves it saying nothing back together the crews dynamic is noticeably warmer ana is less rigid even allowing moments of familiarity with oliver oliver announces progress on the sample and the three share a rare moment of celebration emily feels genuinely fulfilled for the first time she feels she belongs as they resume course to the next planet oliver continues testing one day emily enters the same storage room oliver was in to log planetary data as she prepares to leave she hears a soft irregular blinking curious she removes a covering from a dormant console and finds ivans distress signal still active shaken emily immediately brings ana and oliver to the room she explains that the signal is real and appears to be coming from a nearby planet she insists they investigate and bring ivan back ana shuts it down instantly claiming its a malfunction and turning the signal off when emily presses further ana deflects and urges oliver to back her up his hesitation only deepens emilys suspicion the tension escalates into a heated argument emily accuses them of avoiding the truth under pressure oliver lets something slip just enough to make everyone pause ana freezes emily realises the horrifying implication ivan didnt disappear he was left behind on purpose ana snaps ordering emily to drop it instead emily uses her control of the ship i told you it was important to lock ana and oliver out of the ships navigation and control systems isolating command access she refuses to restore control until they tell her the full truth forced into a corner ana and oliver explain their version of events they describe ivan as unstable obsessed with studying a dangerous alien species on a planet they previously visited unwilling to abandon his research even when ordered they admit they left him there intentionally ana frames it as a necessary decision portraying ivan as recklesspossibly delusional fragmented flashbacks accompany their explanation emily is devastated the betrayal cuts deepest with ana after their seemingly heart to heart she demands they go back for ivan ana refuses outright when emily declares she will go alone ana physically blocks her the argument turns violent the two fight through the ship colliding with equipment and causing damage oliver attempts to intervene but is injured in the chaos emily breaks free and reaches an evacuation pod ana pounds on the door first appealing to logic then to emotion growing increasingly desperate and manipulative emily realizes too late that the pod requires external authorization to launch outside oliver stands at the control his hand near the button that launches the pod ana begs him not to press it emily silently pleads from behind the glass after a long unbearable moment oliver presses the button he chooses this out of his own agency not panic the pod launches emily does not restore control to the ship ana and oliver are left stranded powerless as emily disappears into space the remainder of the act follows emily alone she pilots the pod toward ivans last known location arriving nearly out of rations the planet is eerie almost horror like as she explores grotesque figures emerge creatures that resemble dead humans terrified emily runs panics and falls alone hurt and starving she spirals into regret convinced ana was right and that this was a mistake then she collides with someone emily looks up standing over her is ivanalive battered feral with fear act three ends act four opens in the immediate aftermath of emilys escape on the spaceship there is no explosion of anger only silence ana leans against the glass wall where the evacuation pod once was oliver stands frozen near the launch button for a long moment neither speaks oliver finally tries to say something but ana cuts him off quietly why did you do that her voice is fragile almost broken oliver cant answer she asks again when he still says nothing ana crosses the space between them grabs him by the collar and the tension finally breaks they argue violently not just about emily but about years of unspoken guilt shared responsibility and choices neither of them fully owned all relating to leaving ivan on the planet both end up crying panicked by the realization that they no longer have full control of the ship the argument ends unresolved with ana storming out and oliver left alone in the cockpit the story cuts to the planet emily encounters ivan who thinks shes attacking him and starts attacking her out of self defence she manages to calm him down just long enough to explain who she is but before anything meaningful can be said emily collapses from exhaustion and hunger while unconscious she drifts through fragmented dreams tied to her past traumas her coworker and stuff with her parents when she wakes she finds herself in ivans crude hideout ivan is physically present but emotionally distant muttering to himself studying the evacuation pod blueprint emily carried asking technical questions but refusing to explain anything about how he ended up here she notices that his fingers are blue and one of his eyes are black he is clearly unstable emily begins to doubt herself wondering if ana was right about him after all hoping to gain leverage or understanding emily leaves to search for the evacuation pod that ivan is interested in while doing so she stumbles across a large abandoned structure and realizes with shock that this planet was also studied by humans confused and unsettled she enters the building inside she encounters the planets aliens discovering they are sentient and communicate with one another in a language eerily similar to human speech fragments of russian chinese and english blended together she hides trying to escape unnoticed but eventually finds herself in a room filled with old human equipment and recorded tapes the creatures discover her this time they dont immediately attack one of them visibly less deteriorated than the others speaks to her in english emily is stunned as they speak with emily asking the alien questions another creature enters the room far more decayed and suddenly becomes violent attacking emily emily flees into an adjacent projection room and locks herself inside trapped she plays the tapes emily discovers the truth these are not aliens they are humans grotesquely mutated by longterm exposure to the planets atmosphere and an incurable virus that slowly erodes the brain causing aggression as it progresses the recordings reveal a secret program from world war three run by the director anas father which placed prisoners political enemies and expendable civilians on distant planets to test survivability the program was designed as a contingency plan for global collapse when earth was devastated by a nuclear strike and communication broke down the program was abandoned and eventually repurposed as the current program emily is working in the humans on these planets were left behind to die emily breaks she vomits collapses and sobs overwhelmed by the realization that the mission she believed in is built on atrocity suddenly ivan appears and forcibly pulls her from the building outside emily is silent barely responsive ivan finally begins to talk haltingly as if confessing something hes been carrying alone he explains that he tried to help the people here but failed the infection is incurable the most aggressive among them attacked him forcing him to amputate his own leg to survive he explains that when they landed he ivan wasnt obsessed about there being aliens but rather hellbent on exposing the truth about the atrocities committed here ana refused she claimed ignorance saying her father told her the program used volunteers who were safely returned but ultimately admitted she couldnt allow her fathers reputation to be destroyed oliver hesitated conflicted urging caution rather than action when a crisis arose near the ship ana made a choice she left ivan behind oliver resisted then gave in he talks about ana and oliver briefly however emily is shattered by this she insists they have to help the people on the planet no matter the cost ivan warns her its dangerous and likely futile but emily doesnt care anymore she returns to the building and promises the survivors that she will expose the truth ivan hesitates then follows meanwhile back on the ship ana and oliver appear again in brief tense scenes threaded through the act they are barely speaking oliver attempts distraction avoidance anything to keep from confronting what theyve done but it fails eventually ana focuses on the practical problem navigation using her experience as a pilot she discovers a way to reroute the ship using previously traveled pathways even without full control her first instinct is to leave to put as much distance between themselves and the planet as possible oliver stops her he argues not emotionally but simplythat leaving is worse worse than staying worse than facing ivan worse than facing emily ana doesnt respond at first eventually she changes course the ship redirects moving back toward the planet the act ends with the spaceship approaching the planet from orbit while on the surface emily and ivan begin forming a plan ivan remains hesitant and deeply afraid emily is resolute no longer concerned with her own safety only with the truth act five opens with a flashback from olivers point of view revealing what truly happened the day he ana and ivan first landed on the planet they find the humans and the humans tell them everything ivan wants to expose the company ana however is more hesitant the two argue and it results in ana leaving the planet with oliver actively choosing to leave ivan behind the focus is on olivers silence and complicity contextualising his guilt and setting the emotional tone for the act the story then cuts to the present ana and oliver land on the planet following emilys tracker oliver leads for the first time taking initiative while ana remains withdrawn and silent allowing him control he suggests they stay together no matter what ana quietly agrees though she knows its already too latetheir bond fractured the moment she abandoned ivan meanwhile emily and ivan locate the evacuation pod ivan confirms he can repair it though it will take time which allows them to properly gather evidence during this process emily finally realises that ivan is infected with the same degenerative virus affecting the planets human inhabitants details shed previously noticed but never connected ivan is resigned to it emily is not she insists they will find a cure once they return to earth ivan challenges her motivations asking why shes sacrificing everything for this emily answers that its the right thing to do but when pressed for something deeper she has no response they are interrupted by movement both freeze as ana and oliver emerge the four stand in silence emily is shocked and deeply hurt at the sight of ana though she masks it ivan is openly terrified oliver is hit with the full weight of guilt at how broken emily and ivan look ana feels it too though she cant articulate it oliver is the first to speak apologising directly to ivan when he steps forward ivan recoils ready to flee but emily stops him oliver backs away respecting the boundary emily then states plainly that she knows everything and intends to fix it ana attempts to say theyre there to help speaking in detached impersonal terms but emily shuts her down telling her shes done enough damage ivan suggests leaving altogether but emily instead decides that ana and oliver need to see the consequences she brings them back to the research facility inside ana and oliver confront the mutated humans and the evidence left behind both are visibly shaken ana admits she never knew the full extent of the program again and while emily believes her she makes it clear that ana still enabled the system that allowed it to happen emily shows them the tapes oliver breaks down finally realising that his silence was a choice and a wrong one he offers to help apologising through tears ana remains quiet emotionally shut down emily assigns oliver and ivan to organise and secure the logs while she records anas testimony she tells ivan theyll use the spaceship instead of the evacuation pod allowing them to transport both evidence and survivors still wary emily keeps copies of the logs herself as ivan and oliver work together they talk oliver apologises without asking for forgiveness ivan doesnt forgive him but he listens its not reconciliation but it is honesty emily confronts ana alone their conversation is raw and brutal ana initially lashes out defensively then collapses under the weight of it all finally admitting the atrocities she let happen some of the humans speak to her as well angry but clear that her father bears the greatest responsibility with the evidence secured emily announces theyre leaving using the ship oliver agrees immediately ana says nothing panic simmering beneath the surface ivan then reveals he is staying behind some of the humans will stay too he believes there is nothing left for him on earth and that the infection will kill him regardless emily argues desperately that a cure is possible ivan refuses quietly admitting that he no longer wants to be cured ana finally speaks trying to reach him ivan snaps back that thanks to her hes realised how disposable his life always was the moment is framed not as justice but as a deep injustice something said that cannot be taken back ana breaks desperate for control she declares they are not leaving she says she wants things to go back to how they were that she hates herself for destroying the only happiness shes ever known she threatens the logs but no one truly believes shell go through with it emily pulls ana aside into the log room and tells her to stopaccept that actions have consequences ana responds by turning the confrontation physical the two fight brutally emotionally without restraint emily overpowers ana pinning her down and choking her as ana repeats that she gives up that shell give them the ship emily doesnt stop until she remembers her coworker her parents the cycle of violence its shown here that emily may be the reason her father died her father was highly abusive and emily retliated against it by smashing a bottle on his head in self defense he left the house and never came back she thinks back on this moment and she releases ana emily takes what she needs and prepares to leave ana behind oliver intervenes hysterical but resolute insisting ana must come back as she is evidence herself reluctantly emily agrees they leave the planet with the logs survivors oliver ana and emily ivan stays behind in the aftermath the truth is exposed at first the public is split the company tries to cover everything up people dont believe it but then videos and photos are shown the director is arrested along with the companys leadership new scientific teams take over olivers sample becomes the foundation for restoring earths ecosystem a slow process but a real one oliver testifies accepting the fallout that comes with it he stays with the company to help with the sample ana testifies as well she is stripped of her titles reputation and power everything she built is gone emily reunites with her family and dedicates herself to rebuilding the earth developing machines that restore soil and ecosystems ten years later earth is visibly recovering emily thrives professionally though she carries a quiet heaviness after a day at work she unexpectedly runs into oliver they share coffee reminisce and speak of the past emily admits she doesnt know what became of ivan oliver hesitates then reveals that he only came to ask that she talk to ana who sits on her deathbed emily is upset at this at the fact that oliver and ana are still in contact but after some convincing she agrees to think on it oliver asks to remain in contact but emily doesnt answer emily visits ana a few days later they speak through a glass wall as anas disease is infectious they talk briefly awkwardly the exchange ends with emily saying she enjoyed their time together but she cannot have ana in her life again and emily leaves even while ana weakly asks her not to the story ends with emily at work she sees a sprouting plant in the soil she looks at it her expression neutral before smiling softly and turning away continuing her work after reading through all of that its pretty bad but i dont know its still worth a try to get feedback

tripod accessories you didnt know you needed when photographers think about improving their gear cameras and lenses usually come first however tripod accessories are often overlooked especially by beginners many new photographers believe that buying a tripod alone is enough to achieve stability and better shots in reality the right tripod accessories can significantly enhance usability comfort and image quality these accessories not only solve common shooting problems but also help photographers adapt to different environments and shooting styles more efficiently as photography skills grow so do creative ambitions whether you are shooting landscapes portraits videos or night photography tripod accessories can make your setup more versatile and professional understanding which accessories truly add value can help you get more out of your tripod without unnecessary spending surprisingly some of the most useful accessories are small affordable and often unknown to beginners why tripod accessories matter more than you think to begin with tripod accessories exist to solve realworld shooting challenges while a tripod provides basic stability accessories improve precision flexibility and safety for example even a slight vibration caused by wind or uneven ground can ruin a longexposure shot accessories help eliminate these issues and ensure consistent results moreover accessories allow you to adapt one tripod for multiple purposes a simple accessory can turn a photography tripod into a video rig a travelfriendly setup or a macro photography tool this versatility is especially important for beginners who may not want to invest in multiple tripods for different needs in fact experienced photographers often say that accessories extend the life and usefulness of their tripod more than upgrading the tripod itself another important reason accessories matter is comfort shooting for long hours can be physically demanding accessories that improve ergonomics reduce strain and allow you to focus on creativity instead of discomfort over time this can directly impact learning speed and shooting consistency essential tripod accessories that improve stability and safety one of the most underrated tripod accessories is the tripod weight hook or center column hook many tripods include this feature but beginners often ignore it hanging a camera bag or weight from the hook increases stability by lowering the center of gravity this is particularly useful in windy conditions or while shooting long exposures even lightweight tripods can perform much better with added weight another important accessory is tripod feet or spikes standard rubber feet work well on smooth indoor surfaces but they can slip on grass sand snow or rocky terrain interchangeable spike book review a city on mars can we settle space should we settle space and have we really thought this through by by kelly weinersmith zach weinersmith there has been speculation and excitement about colonizing mars for decades with much more fervor recently this book written by a selfproclaimed science geek couple lays out the practical difficulties of achieving that goal anytime soon the authors do not question the wisdom of expanding our frontiers but argue that irrational exuberance about this endeavor has obscured the significant challenges that make it unrealistic for the foreseeable future they examine a variety of critical areasthe reality behind the promise of space riches in minerals the challenges of scaling energy and equipment needed to achieve it the complexities of food production and other essentials for sustaining a colony the fragility of the human body and medical complications and issues with laws and governance while many of us might superficially grasp these issues the book presents them in a digestible manner that not only highlights the challenges but also enhances our appreciation of the endeavor among the areas explored the discussion on space governance was particularly new and insightful for me the authors outline the current state of space governance or lack thereof draw from historical experiences of humans governing new frontiers and offer some suggestions overall their view is that beyond acknowledging the hurdles ahead we should prioritize rigorous experimentation here on earth to improve our chances though the issues they discuss could be dense in other hands the authors use wit and humor and it works remarkably well i listened to an audiobook this book was quite enjoyable and is an interesting and valuable take on an important area of popular science

supporting lgbtqia older adults clips from one of my subscriptions the carlat geriatric psychiatry report carlat take lgbtqia older adults face distinct and often overlooked risks especially related to autonomy identity and safety factors like age gender identity sexual orientation race and disability interact with systems that were not built to support their needs ask about pronouns preferred names and key relationships stay alert for red flags such as family interference pressure to stop gac or mistreatment framed as protection dont assume silence means safety create space for honest conversation document preferences clearly and speak up when care systems fall short affirming identity isnt just best practice its part of your clinical responsibility supporting lgbtqia older adults gender and sexuality gender and sexuality may be explored at any age ask about important relationships using genderneutral language dont overlook bisexual patientstheyre often ignored in clinical settings and face higher rates of isolation and worse medical and mental health outcomes lampe et al 2024 ask intersex clients about childhood surgeries and their experiences with gender and sexualitythis signals safety and openness to disclosure sexual activity in older adults can raise complicated feelings in caregivers in institutional settings follow policies regarding consensual sexual relationships if you are concerned a patient is being penalized for their sexuality or gender expression raise it directly with staff or through a compliance hotline for patients living with family ask how they manage privacy and mutual respect around intimacy always ask about nonconsensual encounters satisfaction with sexual activity and understanding of sti risk in private practice settings inclusive imagery like photos of samesex couples or genderdiverse expression can send a clear signal that your care is welcoming most importantly in all settings practice cultural humility and be willing to learn

how to be cool af the psychologybacked lessons no one talks about spent months digging into the science of charisma reading everything from social psychology research to books by communication experts talked to people i considered genuinely cool analyzed what made them magnetic heres what actually works not the recycled be confident garbage you see everywhere turns out being cool isnt about trying hard its about unlearning the anxious patterns most of us develop society conditions us to seek approval constantly which ironically makes us less attractive the cool people theyve somehow bypassed that trap coolness is emotional steadiness most people are reactive as hell someone criticizes them they defend immediately someone doesnt text back they panic cool people have what psychologists call emotional regulation they dont let external stuff dictate their internal state this comes from the charisma myth by olivia fox cabane shes a stanford lecturer who breaks down charisma into learnable behaviors the book won multiple awards and completely changed how i understood social dynamics what stuck with me most was her explanation of presence truly listening without planning your next sentence most conversations are just two people waiting to talk when you actually listen you become magnetic this is the best practical charisma book ive ever read insanely applicable stuff practice this next conversation focus entirely on what the other person is saying dont rehearse responses notice how differently people react to you stop seeking validation the fastest way to kill your coolness is caring too much what others think research from social psychology shows that perceived neediness is one of the biggest attraction killers cool people validate themselves started using an app called finch to build this habit its a self care app where you raise a little bird by completing daily goals sounds silly but it gamifies self validation you get rewards for taking care of yourself rather than seeking external approval the psychological shift is subtle but powerful after a few weeks noticed way less anxiety in social situations because wasnt constantly scanning for approval signals develop genuine interests cool people are passionate about weird specific things theyre not trying to like whats trendy they genuinely geek out over something could be vintage motorcycles fermentation obscure music genres whatever the courage to be disliked by ichiro kishimi explores this through adlerian psychology the core idea is that most unhappiness comes from trying to meet others expectations the book sold over 35 million copies in japan and challenges everything you think about relationships and social dynamics one insight that hit me all problems are interpersonal relationship problems your anxiety about being cool thats you imagining other peoples judgments when you stop living for others approval you become naturally magnetic this book will make you question everything you think you know about social acceptance master comfortable silence uncool people fill every gap with nervous chatter cool people are comfortable with silence theres actual neuroscience behind this silence creates space for deeper connection and shows youre not anxious check out charisma on command on youtube charlie houpert breaks down body language and conversation skills using clips of celebrities and public figures his video on how to never run out of things to say changed how to handle awkward pauses instead of panicking learned to embrace the silence or ask deeper follow up questions the channel has over 6 million subscribers for good reason its practical social skills training disguised as entertainment build competence in something nobody respects someone whos all talk cool people are genuinely good at something could be anything cooking coding skateboarding woodworking competence breeds quiet confidence befreed is an aipowered learning app built by columbia alumni and former google engineers that turns books research papers and expert talks into personalized audio podcasts type in what you want to learn like building social confidence or mastering conversation skills and it creates a custom learning plan just for you what makes it different is the depth control start with a 10minute summary of something like the charisma myth and if it clicks switch to a 40minute deep dive with examples and real stories the voice options are weirdly addictive too theres this sarcastic narrator that makes dense psychology research actually entertaining plus theres freedia an ai coach you can chat with midpodcast to ask questions or get book recommendations based on your goals way easier than trying to read everything yourself when building new skills start small with any skill pick one thing and practice it deliberately for 30 minutes daily use an app like insight timer to build the meditation habit of focused practice its primarily a meditation app with over 100000 guided sessions but works great for timing focused skill building sessions the act of showing up daily even when you dont feel like it builds the self respect that makes you cool stop trying to impress this is the paradox the moment you try to be cool youre not cool is a side effect of being secure enough to not care about being cool listen to the overwhelmed brain podcast with paul colaianni hes a former software engineer turned emotional intelligence coach his episodes on people pleasing and boundary setting are game changers episode 437 on becoming the version of you that you want to be explains why trying to impress others always backfires you end up shapeshifting into whoever you think they want which is exhausting and inauthentic people sense that inauthenticity immediately the research backs this up studies on social perception show that authenticity is rated as more attractive than competence or warmth being genuinely yourself flaws and all beats any performance reality check none of this works overnight it took like 8 months to stop being anxious in social situations some days still catch myself seeking validation or trying too hard but the tools above gave a framework the more you practice emotional steadiness pursue genuine interests and stop performing the more naturally cool you become not because youre trying to be cool because you stopped trying

tomt mid90s macintosh cdrom pointandclick edutainment game inspired by rendezvous with rama hi all ive been haunted by the memory of a mid90s macintosh cdrom edutainment game i can remember a ton of odd details about but not the name ive flicked through the entire education section of the macintosh garden to no avail heres what i remember the game is a firstperson pointandclick adventure in prerendered 3d environments with some prerendered 3d cutscenes your character is an astronaut flying to meet an alien spaceship a la rendezvous with rama the alien ship had a bluish kind of spoonshaped hull kind of like star treks voyager but smoother and without nacelles before boarding you choose one of three armored space suits that are all basically identical the game is firstperson through the spacesuits visor with a big trapezoidal back button in the centrebottom of the screen once aboard the alien ship you explore three rooms full of science experiments and human artifacts one room contains a terrarium where the player must adjust sunlight flora and fauna to achieve a sustainable ecology another room contains a human spacesuit that plays a recording of i since learned astronaut charlie duke describing how he fell over during the lunar olympics of apollo 16 i remember him saying if i split my suit open im dead and describing how his fear subsided as he got to his feet and listened to the fans and pumps of the suit once youve explored all the rooms youre ordered to get back to your own ship and evacuate the final cutscene shows the alien ship drifting away pulsing with green light amid chatter from mission control the screen fills with green lightning the scene cuts to black and the game ends

what did 2025 quietly changed about how we think and work the year our tools time and relationships got quietly rewired big picture snapshot 2025 didnt feel like a revolution but it quietly rewrote the defaults for how people think work and relate the real story of how 2025 changed how we work isnt about flashy headlinesits about subtle shifts ai becoming a normal coworker hybrid becoming the unspoken norm and people retreating from loud public feeds into smaller safer circles underneath it all sits a growing preoccupation with mental energy rather than just time and output this piece explores those shifts so you can name what youve been feeling all yearand use it more deliberately in 2026 1 ai moved from future thing to everyday coworker if 20232024 were about talking about ai 2025 was the year people just started using it and stopped making a big deal out of it surveys now show almost half of workers say they use ai at least a few times a year at work with around one in ten using it dailystill a minority but no longer a fringe habit gallupcom companies have poured money into ai yet only a tiny fraction feel theyre truly mature in how they use it suggesting the tech arrived faster than leadership playbooks mckinsey company the quiet psychological shift many knowledge workers now think in drafts first draft by ai second by them people arent just asking what should i write but what should i ask the quality of your prompt is slowly becoming as important as the quality of your writing in the same way that knowing how to search once became as important as knowing who to ask in practice 2025 nudged us into three new mental habits treating ai like a junior colleague you need to supervise expecting some tasks summaries outlines rough code research scans to be aifirst by default worrying and hoping about job impact at the same timemore than half of workers report feeling worried about future ai use at work even as many see its upside pew research center1 like spreadsheets in the 80s ai in 2025 stopped being a topic and became infrastructurestill imperfect but assumed to be in the room 2 hybrid work stopped being a perk and became a boundary by 2025 hybrid wasnt a radical experiment anymoreit was the default setting for millions of remotecapable jobs data this year showed a plateau roughly half of such workers are hybrid about 30 fully remote and 20 fully onsite with remote days hovering around 29 of all paid workdays in the us aura insights other global studies show a similar tilt far fewer people are fully remote than in 2022 but hybrid arrangements have surged cisco newsroom1 the quiet change in how we think about work is this flexibility is no longer a shiny benefitits table stakes in multiple surveys sizable chunks of workers say that if flexible work were taken away theyd start job hunting demand higher pay or even quit outright owl labs flexibility has become a boundary not a bonus realworld example picture a midsized software company in chicago in 2022 their hybrid policy was branded as a progressive perk posters town halls glossy internal decks in 2025 leadership tried to quietly roll back to four mandatory office days the result exit interviews started echoing the same phrase its not the commute its the control recruiters from competitors used hybrid as a wedgewere 23 days you choose which the company didnt just lose people it learned that calendar control was now part of compensation 2025 didnt kill the office it reframed it the office is now a toolfor collaboration onboarding and relationshipbuildingrather than the unquestioned center of work people started planning their weeks around energy and focus what do i need quiet for where do i need people instead of badge swipes 3 mental health moved from issue to everyday constraint another undertheradar shift mental health isnt just a wellness topic its now a core variable in how people choose jobs schedules and relationships recent workplace polls show around half of workers reporting moderate to severe levels of burnout depression or anxiety mindsharepartners yet many hesitate to label themselves as struggling and almost half worry about being judged if they share those struggles at work nami among gen z and millennialsthe bulk of the emerging workforcemental health is cited as a top factor in career decisions and employer loyalty deloitte in 2025 this translated into subtle but powerful behavioral changes people are more willing to turn down promotions that obviously destroy their health psychologically safe and burnoutaware leaders have become quiet retention superpowers teams are experimenting with nomeeting blocks deeper focus time and explicit norms around availability if the 2010s were about optimizing time 2025 feels like the year people started optimizing emotional bandwidth instead of do i have an hour the question became do i have the mental energy for this 4 relationships went from broadcast to small circles only social media in 2025 looks less like a megaphone and more like a series of living rooms for younger users especially public broadcasting is out private curated spaces are in gen z is increasingly choosing close friends lists private group chats finstas and inviteonly servers over constant posting to the main feed medium brands and communities are noticing the same pattern engagement is shifting toward smaller private online communities where conversations feel safer and more meaningful random the quiet change in how we relate we now assume that real conversations happen in dms group chats and niche communitiesnot on the feed audience is becoming less important than circle trust is being rebuilt in smaller unitsteams group chats microcommunitiesrather than big platforms as a result influence is fragmenting instead of one giant audience many people now have five or ten small overlapping circleswork slack family chat gaming server niche professional community 2025 didnt end social media it turned it inside out bringing it together and what to do with it taken together 2025 quietly shifted the ground under our feet ai became an everyday collaborator hybrid became a baseline expectation mental health became a nonnegotiable constraint and relationships moved into smaller safer circles none of this came with a single headline momentbut you probably feel it in your calendar your chat apps and your energy levels if you want to operate well in this new landscape start asking how can i partner with ai instead of compete with it what flexibility do i actually need to protect my energy where are my small circles and how do i invest in them intentionally thats the work of the next year if this kind of question helps you see your own life more clearly consider following questionclasss questionaday at questionclasscoma daily nudge to keep your thinking sharp and your conversations deeper bookmarked for you here are a few books that deepen the themes 2025 surfaced the burnout challenge by christina maslach michael p leiter a researchbacked look at how work environments create burnout and what leaders and individuals can do to redesign them the lonely century by noreena hertz explores how modern life reshapes connection and why smaller more intentional communities are becoming essential power and prediction by ajay agrawal joshua gans avi goldfarb helps you understand ai not as magic but as a new kind of prediction engine that quietly rewires decisions jobs and value questionstrings to practice questionstrings are deliberately ordered sequences of questions in which each answer fuels the next creating a compounding ladder of insight that drives progressively deeper understanding what to do now use this to audit how 2025 has already changed your work and relationships then adjust your habits and commitments accordingly 2025 shift audit string for when you want to surface the invisible changes in your own life where in my week do i already partner with ai even in small ways what tasks could i delegate or cocreate with ai that i still do manually where do i feel most in control of my time and locationand where do i feel boxed in which relationships or communities actually energize me instead of draining me what is one boundary or habit i can change this month to protect my energy and deepen my best circles try weaving this into a journaling session or a 11 conversation with a trusted colleague its a fast way to turn vague 2025 vibes into specific actionable adjustments in the end 2025 is a reminder that the biggest changes to how we think work and relate rarely arrive with fireworksthey arrive as defaults and the real skill is noticing them in time to choose them on purpose

timeless information dynamics tid how change occurs without time or intention early good morning infonauts weve had a lot of discussion on invariants and how they are fundamental to the basic backbone of the infonautology framework several recent comments have converged on the next natural question if coherence specifies the conditions under which a system remains the same system then what accounts for change itself what makes systems transform if we dont appeal to observers intention or even time as a primitive this is where the next layer of the framework comes in which i refer to as timeless information dynamics tid the motivation for tid is simple but subtle most models of change assume time first then describe how states evolve within it but that approach quietly presupposes that identity is already welldefined across moments in earlier posts ive focused on coherence as a viability condition that is the minimal set of relational constraints that must remain invariant for something to count as the same system across transformation tid picks up after that question is settled in tid change is not something initiated by an observer a measurement or an external clock instead transformations are understood as movements within a constrained informational space defined by those identitypreserving relations a systems possible transformations are limited by its structure what we call dynamics is simply the exploration of that admissible space ie the set of all transformations a system can undergo while still remaining that system or everything the systems structure permits without losing identity from this perspective observers are not drivers of change they are particular coherent trajectories within the same space of transformations measurement interaction and intervention are themselves transformations subject to the same coherence constraints as everything else nothing special happens at observation it is just one path among many this is why the framework is called timeless time is not denied but it is not treated as fundamental ordering duration and causality emerge once coherent trajectories a sequence of admissible transformations a system undergoes while preserving identity are traced and compared to compare trajectories means to place two or more such sequences in relation and ask questions like which changes happened before others which persisted longer which depended on which these are the relations that give rise to timelike notions what exists prior to that is not before in a temporal sense but structurally prior a space of possible transformations constrained by identity conditions ordering duration and causality dont exist by default rather they emerge when multiple coherent trajectories are related to one another time therefore as proposed emerges when stable patterns of change can be related to one another without comparison there is change but no ordering duration or causality so to summarize this coherence tells us which transformations still count as preserving a systems identity tid asks how movement through that admissible space occurs without assuming intention agency or time as a primitive this separation matters because it avoids a common conceptual problem systems dont usually fail because change stops they fail because identity can no longer be preserved under the transformations they undergo thats when we see fragmentation forking or category failure rather than smooth decay at this stage tid is intentionally preformal the aim is not to replace physics information theory or dynamical systems but to make explicit the structural assumptions those frameworks already rely on in mature cases these ideas should collapse into familiar mathematical objects equivalence classes admissible transformations invariance structures and eventually domainspecific dynamics that is certainly above my paygrade for now the guiding idea is simply this change does not require a driver it requires structure and identity does not require time it requires coherence im sharing this as a first pass not a finished theory therefore questions critiques and pressuretesting are very welcome especially around where this framing clarifies things and where it breaks thanks for reading and for helping refine this work through dialogue m1o rinfonautology

where does foresight actually fit in the dragon city meta design discussion over the last few posts i shared several dragon concepts built around a mechanic i called foresight instead of introducing another dragon i wanted to step back and explain where this mechanic would actually live inside the current dragon city meta and how it interacts with existing playstyles this isnt meant as a replacement for spiked shields silences or dodge its rather a different axis entirely design philosophy foresight is not meant to be a hardcontrol mechanic it exists to shift pressure from stop the opponent to act with certainty dragon city already has denial silence avoidance dodge guards raw pressure doom crits foresight explores a different space delayed inevitability visible consequences decision pressure instead of randomness what foresight is and isnt foresight delays the outcomes of by 1 turn revealing what will happen before it resolves the delayed outcome is guaranteed to occur next turn players get a reaction window instead of immunity to plan how to manipulatebend the outcomes in their own favor foresight is about information and commitment not denial the 2 kinds of achievable foresight passive foresight applies only to specialskill outcomes and familydefining passive triggers and it does not affect basic attacks or universal combat modifiers active foresight only works for a certain amount of turns when its applied via active skill without relying on opponents actions active foresight for a certain time applies to every attack used by opposing dragon regardless of it being a special skill or not how foresight interacts with common meta archetypes 1burst oneturn kill kits critical crew highdamage skills still hit they are simply delayed by 1 turn the defending player can respond knowing the damage is coming effect passive critical triggers are less unpredictable and more resistable either by blocking or switching out to redirect the damage 2 dodge evasion karmasevaders dodge checks still apply when the delayed effect resolves foresight doesnt bypass evasion or neutralization mechanics effect dodge remains valuable foresight doesnt invalidate but reconditions it 3 extra turn tempo chains hpsduo family extra turns are delayed not removed the tempo advantage still exists but its visible in advance effect tempo is delayed not shut down 4 self healing sustain healing becomes reactive instead of reflexive you heal knowing exactly whats about to land effect sustain requires planning instead of guessing 5 switching team play delayed outcomes are tied to the skill not the dragon switching can mitigate consequences but not erase them effect encourages team coordination over panic swaps discussion would a delayedoutcome mechanic add depth or slow the game too much would you rather face foresight than hard denial like silence or stun which archetype do you think benefits most from foresight burst control or sustain
