15 retro games for 2025 i have a deep nostalgia for retro console gaming starting in the nes era and going up until the ps2 generation games on my list tend to be ones im either revisiting for the first time since childhood or ones i never got the chance to try growing up when it comes to newer titles i lean towards indie games with vintage trappings i profess that modern pixel art makes me weak at the knees for those reasons the list below is a bit of an eclectic mix hope youll find something that piques your interest or jogs an old memory on the cusp xenogears psx i might be courting controversy here starting off with one of the most wellregarded jrpgs at the bottom of the list but for a game i appreciate from afar more than i love wholeheartedly this seems like the appropriate spot its hard to deny the ambition on display with the game tackling serious religious philosophical and existential themes at the same time actually playing the game is a whole other matter in describing xenogears to a friend i told him its like listening to a podcast at 05x speed for about 50 hours and then cranking it up to 4x for the last 10 the pacing is all over the place going from meandering and plodding before abruptly thrusting ahead at warp speed where entire plotlines are skipped over and described only in a star wars text crawl despite its myriad flaws theres much to admire here strong character design interesting battle mechanics and a memorable soundtrack just not more than the sum of its parts for me tactics ogre let us cling together psp as a huge fan of matsunos games particularly final fantasy tactics and vagrant story i went into this with high expectations to say i came away disappointed wouldnt be inaccurate the tone and writing bear a lot in resemblance to final fantasy tactics with political factions and backstabbing machinations around every corner the gameplay though is where things get messy class balance is somewhat absurd with ranged bows dominating heads and shoulders over melee map design is spotty where verticality and height advantage often play too large a factor in outcomes using a guide is nearly mandatory in order to unlock unique characters then having them join you at level 1 and immediately losing access to their special abilities is a cruel prize indeed its clear that this is one of matsunos earlier forays into game development and that he would hone his craft on later titles still worth experiencing to see his formative game design chops on display a tantalizing taste legend of zelda nes with redux patch even with a famicom in the household i never owned legend of zelda as a child when i first played it several years ago wanting to revisit the series roots i found myself continually stumped needing to use a guide to make any semblance of progress it was hard for me to understand why the game seemed to top every list of best nes games given the frequent moments of frustration i encountered this past year i fancied giving the game another shot but not before applying the redux rom hack this fanmade patch strives to make the game more approachable without affecting balance or overall design among other things it sports a fresh localization shows more detail in the minimap marks all bombable walls and burnable bushes and fixes a number of aggravating bugs these qol changes collectively bring the game from relic of history better appreciated as a museum piece to a modern playable affair best of all i didnt need a guide this time around making every heart container located and dungeon cleared that much more gratifying while purists might scoff at this rom hack i wholeheartedly recommend it for anyone venturing into this venerable title for the first time ratchet clank going commando ps2 there are some games that are wellknown for their minimalism where the experience is distilled down into the essence of a few core mechanics ico on the ps2 is one of the best examples and then at the other extreme theres ratchet clank where the motto on the wall at insomiac games mustve been everything and the kitchen sink the way the game yanks you between different gameplay modes gadgets and level types was enough to make my head spin thankfully the majority of game modes pull their weight with the primary gunplay being front and centre ive heard the series described as 3d mega man and its not too far off between the dozen weapons and their upgrades its fun planning and testing the optimal loadout for every stage there are a few frustrating sequences scattered throughout though giant clank sounds fun in theory but is a royal pain to navigate the physics arent precise enough to warrant the 2d platforming sections and the space combat has the problem of a reverse difficulty curve where early levels are punishingly difficult until you upgrade your ship still the core gameplay loop is satisfying enough that it withstands all of its myriad diversions dragon quest iii snes with translation patch its sometimes hard to appreciate what a fresh coat of paint can do the original dragon warrior iii on nes is a dated affair at best perhaps primitive if youre less charitable having played the nes game for the first time a few years ago i found myself appreciating the leaps forward it took for the genre in 1988 while simultaneously wishing i could get to the end faster the super famicom rendition circa 1996 though is an entirely different affair with its magnificent pixel art rivalling anything on the console including final fantasy vi its rearranged soundtrack and its abundance of charm around every corner this remake was the full realization of the ambition the generation prior the redone aesthetics fully immersed me in the world to a degree that the original didnt giving the sense of an epic adventure every step of the way i was invested at any given moment whether that was helping out the local villagers or finding the next artifact to track down zoma i have no doubt that the more recent hd2d release is excellent but for me this snes version may well be the pinnacle of old school dragon quest ducktales nes my fuzzy memories of this game from childhood made me think this was a straightforward platformer with a unique pogo stick mechanic id forgotten that the levels are largely nonlinear encouraging exploration around every bend and hiding plenty of treasure in sneaky places all that treasure collecting is ontheme too because scrooge is one greedy mofo the difficulty is tuned more fairly than most games of the era though i still played on easy this time around to give myself a cushion from wayward flying enemies all in all a highly enjoyable platformer with exquisite pacing theres also that soundtrack the moon theme alone might stack up as one of the best on the nes capcom was on a tear back in those days balatro pc im not nearly as deep into the roguelike deckbuilder genre as many though i can see the appeal id played slay the spire in the past and was a moderate fan of that immediately balatro struck me as cut from the same cloth but streamlined distilled and refined easy to jump into for anyone whos played poker though it takes a while to discern what actually matters for its somewhat byzantine scoring system while its categorized as a roguelike it feels closer to deckbuilding board games circa 2010 like dominion youre largely playing solitaire and not engaging in combat like in slay the spire once i started to understand the core gameplay loop and distinct phases to a game i began accumulating wins with flushbased strategies while i didnt stick with this for more than a week or two balatro deserves its popularity for lowering the barrier to entry for the genre making it a welcoming affair for gamers of all stripes theres something special here mario kart double dash gc were getting to the first of the multiplayer titles on this list games that i enjoyed playing coop with my son and double dash is the gift that keeps on giving everything about this 2003 entry in the venerable series gives its multiplayer mode longevity from its overthetop track design the bombastic aesthetics and colour palette an allstar roster and especially its rollicking pure arcade physics the coop mode is perfect for levelling the playing field ensuring that anyone can take part regardless of skill there are few things more satisfying than leaning into a turn and having your partner punch a foe to coursecorrect your trajectory all while nabbing a koopa shell for their troubles about the only thing holding it back is a lack of track variety while later games would feature both new courses and throwback ones double dash only sports its 16 fresh tracks some of them being clunkers hello dry dry desert makes the desirable track list even shorter still thats the only notable flaw to speak of celeste pc precision technical platformers arent my thing id tried super meat boy back in the day and bounced hard off its punishing difficulty and deliberately gross aesthetic celeste hooked me by bringing an entirely different vibe to the affair with its encouraging tone and relaxing mood the soundtrack was blissful and calming almost reassuring me that i could make those tough jumps the cast of characters was constantly cheering each other on and by proxy making me feel like victory was within reach even though many stages were challenging theres a few that i died 100 times on i felt like the game had my back throughout which made it all the more rewarding when i finally succeeded the visuals are breathtaking making excellent use of saturated colour palettes distinctive pixel art and a sprinkling of particle effects for good measure with a touching story drawn directly from the developers personal struggles this is an incredible affair top to bottom mario party 6 gc speaking of multiplayer mario party isnt a series id ever given much thought not since getting blisters on my hands playing the n64 games at a friends house just a trifle for distraction i always felt but not a serious game imagine my surprise when i learned that the gamecube titles were held in even higher regard than the n64 ones and that theyd introduced coop my son and i lost track of how many games we played or how many times we cackled with glee when cpu luigi took a risky gamble that backfired oh luigi many of the minigames seemed impossible at first but gradually learning then and forming tactics as a team made the payoff of our later victories ever so sweet figuring out when to parlay or save our coins and stars provided for a metalayer of strategy that meant every position in a game felt winnable out of all of the games on this list mario party 6 provided the most bonding moments with my son which puts it in cherished territory eff bowser though fire emblem awakening 3ds having played only the original gba fire emblem and bouncing off many successive sequels id assumed that the series wasnt my jam oil and water between me and tactical rpgs and all that turns out all i needed was for the series to sprinkle a dating sim into the festivities to respark my interest more than that though cranking the knob towards rpgstyle character customization and away from pure tactics a la advance wars gives someone like me plenty to sink my teeth into i appreciated how i could effectively stack any two units at a time finding complementary skillsets to build mega units while lessening the burden of turnbyturn tactical placement to say nothing of the production values which had me hooked between its expressive character portraits charming lowpoly models and pitchperfect score some of the later levels devolved into a zergling rushfest where it seemed like there was no way to avoid being swarmed by enemy reinforcements this occurred more commonly in the late game marring an otherwise excellent experience despite that im already figuring out when to slot this one in for a replay were talking alltime classics marios picross gb for the bulk of the games on this list i marathoned them for days and weeks at a time until i devoured them whole and then theres picross a game i nibbled at in small bites over the course of the year this is a title thats perfectly suited for brief sessions while out and about whether i was riding the subway or waiting at the dentists to be sure theres newer and more involved versions of nonogram everywhere and all sport the addictive qualities inherent to this logic puzzle but for all their advancements i remain drawn to the elegant simplicity of the game boy original the controls are well thought out and suited for portable play moreso than the halfdozen variants ive tried on my phone indeed ive completed both picross and picross 2 for gb over the past few years and am now replaying the first entry in its entirely not unlike tetris on the same system sometimes the initial takes on classic puzzle games remain the most enduring super mario bros 3 snes via super mario allstars every few years i get the itch to replay super mario bros 3 front to back this wasnt possible when i owned this cart on famicom as a child i could warp through the game to reach level 8 sure but without a save system in place there was no feasible way to take a leisurely stroll through all of the worlds between its various rereleases that problem has since been rectified and then some and its vaulted my opinion of this game even higher where it remains my favourite 2d platformer of all time the sheer inventiveness on display throughout its level design is something to behold with no idea ever overstaying its welcome it presents a difficult but fair challenge and its shorter levels in comparison to its follow up super mario world mean that any stage can be overcome with enough persistence and dedication i still find myself smiling when i uncover secrets even when the prize is another suit ill just stash away and never use its influence over modernday platformers still looms large theres clearly a lineage between this and celeste for example with mario 3 the only question is how long before i fire it up for another whirl legend of zelda wind waker gc over the years zelda games have branched off into two camps there are the dungeon games where solving intricate puzzles within dungeons is the focus and progress is gated by specific item unlocks then there are the exploration games where the vast possibilities of an open world beckon you to explore every nook and cranny having only the vaguest memory of my initial playthrough upon release i assumed wind waker was a fairly straightforward followup to the massively successful ocarina of time with interlocking puzzles galore awaiting me i was pleasantly surprised to discover that its identity lay elsewhere and that sailing the vast seas to trawl for doohickeys and thingamabobs was inextricably more rewarding than solving dungeons a big part of wind wakers timelessness comes down to its distinctive art style which if you can believe caused a lot of controversy back in 2003 the impeccable celshaded graphics drew me into this swashbuckling rendition of hyrule and the whimsical playful soundtrack kept me hooked even though there are only a handful of dungeons proper the sense of scale and adventure lead to this being perhaps my favourite 3d zelda title definitely my favourite link a tier all its own ufo 50 pc for nearly three months i was transfixed by ufo 50 throughout that period it impressed me time and again by taking the nostalgia and trappings of a faux retro setting and marrying those to modern game design principles the creativity and execution of games like avianos night manor magic garden and party house were beyond reproach running the gamut of genres across 4x civ builder point click adventure pacman style arcade game and deckbuilder to say nothing of a whole swath of other excellent titles seaside drive mortol onion delivery overbold velgress barbuta no matter your taste theres something here for everyone i had that impression of ufo 50 before i embarked on its 20hour jrpg playing through grimstone brought so much joy and admiration that i felt compelled to write a review covering one game in the collection in short grimstone may represent the pinnacle of retro jrpgs id happily pay for it as a standalone game that i played it after sinking 110 hours into ufo 50 is the cherry on top at my age its not often that i feel awestruck anymore ufo 50 evokes that feeling it makes me step back in wonder at how a team of six put together this tremendous package over a period of eight years for anyone whos in the specific venn diagram intersection of retrogaming nerd and pixelartbased indie game enthusiast ufo 50 represents a onceinalifetime phenomenon a painstakingly handcrafted collection thats unlikely to be attempted again im glad i found it when i did

the cathedral and the bazaar a philosophicalpolitical reflection ver 20 the text is based on the premise that politics is an information system analogous to programming just as the opensource development process established a new more resilient paradigm in software the text explores the meaning and consequences of applying that paradigm to the political process the current political crisis is interpreted as a clash between closed ideological systems and an open information environment its futurological dimension lies in the claim that future politics must operate as an open iterative system in order to remain sustainable eric raymonds cult essay is often described as a manifesto of an organizational paradigm in the opensource programming world although raymond primarily deals with practical advice and tricks for successfully managing opensource projects his key metaphorthe difference between the cathedral and the bazaaralso offers a broader philosophical and political dimension it becomes a fertile basis for comparing the old ideologies of the preinformational era which relied on predefined frameworks with contemporary models based on continuous contextualization of phenomena in programming cathedrals represent monumental closed projects that function as long as they remain within a hermetically sealed system any opening examination or hacking is perceived as a threat to their stability this is why linus torvalds utters his famous sentence given enough eyeballs all bugs are shallow in other words when there are enough observers problems become trivial in closed systems where the perspective comes from a single narrow niche problems remain invisible in open ones they surface and demand to be resolved in a similar way the ideologies of the preinformational era did not arise within a broad heterogeneous space but within small mutually indoctrinated circles they defined the boundaries of reality in advance they determined what may be thought what is true which interpretations are allowed and which are not such ideologies functioned like a hammer for which every social phenomenon was a nail they did not allow continuous determination of the frameworkon the contrary the predefined framework was untouchable in contrast todays era enables constant and uninterrupted contextualization today we are exposed daily to dozens and hundreds of people with different experiences perspectives and background matrices every text position or idea is immediately subjected to a multitude of viewpoints the bazaar is permanently open for comparison in marxs time this was not possiblemarx was confined to small groups of mutually indoctrinated collaborators and occasional random observers but the same mechanism marked all ideologues of that era they created systems that were not the product of a broad unpredictable spectrum of ideas and people but of a closed circle of authority this is why today we clearly see how certain groupingslibertarian communist religious feminist hegelianstruggle to survive on the open stage what happens is analogous to the public release of a programs source code at the very moment of publication the entire code collapses because it is full of holes and misalignments with its primary security requirements of sustainability the political equivalent is a rupture upon contact with reality old ideologues enter the space of open contextualization but it does not suit them cathedrals of thought that rest on a narrow spectrum of experience and predefined explanations crack when subjected to dynamic questioning their promoters are no longer respected figures from the perspective of the bazaar but ordinary ridicules their foundations were not built for terrain that constantly reexamines its own boundaries and does not tolerate a disconnect from reality from this follows todays political crisis the paradigm of open contextualization in which we all already participate is incompatible with a political system that still operates according to the principles of closed codeaccording to the logic of predefined frameworks and predetermined answers the consequence is a loss of credibility and legitimacy of political institutions and entire narratives the informational revolution the internet and the free flow of information have made the framework openand thus unavoidable closed code of course has its advantages it is fast efficient and does not require questioning but in the long run open systems produce more stable results the same applies to politics closed groupingsfeminists conservatives communists libertariansstill occasionally generate a strong impulse but it is shortlived and undemanding they cannot create a mass affirmative movement because they rest on immutable frameworks that disintegrate when confronted with a broader spectrum of perspectives this is precisely why they do not represent a solution to the crisisthey are its carriers the open process although slower in initiating power rests on flexible and repeatedly renegotiated foundations it rejects dogma demands verification of starting assumptions and allows small but stable ideological structures to spread and strengthen without collapse and where are we as a civilization we are in the bazaarin the space of open contextualization and anyone who wants to succeed in such a space must understand its logic on the political bazaar we find a whole range of defenders of predefined truths which to everyone outside their narrow frameworks appear strange or even grotesque such actors do not gain broad appeal they can gather a small group of followers but they cannot become dominant because they cannot survive under conditions of shifting and multiple perspectives in contrast there are individuals and groups who accept an eclectic mix of approaches experiences and interpretations they strive to build common foundations that can withstand openness and constant reinterpretationa political code that can be sustained in an environment without predefined boundaries people who understand that there is no unquestionable truth people who are willing to continuously reexamine their own positions and shape a framework through encounters with others can today finally create a political solution that was not previously possible technological conditions finally allow thisjust as open source enabled a new era in programming the solution to the political crisis therefore lies in optimizing agreement within the paradigm of open contextualization the alternative is an attempt to abolish the open frameworkshutting down the internet restricting the flow of information rebuilding walls but technological changes and technological revolutions are unstoppable once information becomes free and so we really have no choice but to build a world aligned with the zeitgeist of the digital age

ones i have posted but i wanted to put this here anyways its a thing i posted on my instagram last week when it was my 6 month anniversary of being obsessed with the backrooms where i reflect on how much they have come to mean to me december 20th is 6 months since i became obsessed with the backrooms those who dont know me irl may not realise that i am so new to the backrooms phenomenon im not sure of when i first considered myself a fan but its probably when i went from just listening to a podcast about the extended universe to also reading the wikis as i was getting more intrigued and wanted to find out more so that was around a month earlier on may 24 sometimes it feels like it was only yesterday that i discovered these monoyellow walls and the amazing universe that lies within the excitement i feel in relation to the backrooms is still like i only just got into it and with there being so much ive yet to discover i still have a sense of adventure when coming across levels i arent familiar with yet other times i feel ive been a backrooms fan for so long the familiarity of it all i truly feel that i was meant to eventually discover the backrooms it was only a matter of time the realisation of my love of liminal spaces has been confounding on me where many see regular places i see beauty some people feel uncomfortable with liminal spaces but for me it is the opposite i feel so calm when at some of these spaces while other times i am so happy to be there and even more so if it is a place that i can explore a whole different emotion washes over me the connections i have had to liminal spaces throughout my life that i have now realised visiting these places has always been with me since i was a child with memories of exploring these places with my brother a fascination of such in games and other media my love of urban exploration and abandoned places since i was a teen an appreciation of unique architecture and old buildings these things werent my main interest but they were always adjacent or in the background ive developed such a fascination with what i call backrooms experienceswhich is something i dont think many fans are interested in or even believe in but its the possibility of a backrooms type place existing separate to the fictional realm i want to keep exploring this and learning about dream realms and other ways that people have found these types of places and with the backrooms movie coming out next year im beyond excited to see the backrooms on the big screen the movie will take the backrooms beyond being just an internet phenomenon internet horror i really feel it has the potential to capture the imagination of others as it has myself as it is truly a unique horror concept i cant wait to see what kane parsons has in store for us and i definitely need to get my website online its taken a lot longer than i thought due to having to research a lot of things and now there seems to be new things i want to add to it recently i decided to add a subsite just for the movie as theres so much info to cover on it already my love for the backrooms isnt going anywhere and the adventure and happiness it brings me is something i feel i really needed in my life the backrooms where im meant to be

friend watched in order of andor r1 ot so i recently decided to have my friend watch andor frankly because i just wanted to watch it again and she took some interest as well because she had never seen star wars after anh she mentioned to me that she thought it would have been very weird to not watch andor and r1 to go straight to anh she said she was glad we started with the tv show as a precursor because everything flows so smoothly as we finished anh i mentioned that we were gonna watch esb and rotj she had no idea what else there could be to explore in this story when she said this it actually hit me esb and rotj are literally just extras when you consider andor and r1 its almost strange to realize she really liked esb and was surprised when she found out the truth about vader i didnt actually realize she didnt even know that i forgot to mention that we watched the despecialized editions so georges changes were not present at all i never seen this version until now but i found myself really enjoying the structure the battle at the end of anh was a bit slower but it wasnt bad i actually really liked the original emperor in esb because hes shrouded in so much darkness this reveal was actually very impacting because you hear so much about him in andor that hes just an ominous figure this actually made his appearance in rotj pivotal the second death star didnt actually feel that forced this time around we discussed this and it strangely just flows better because it shows the empire will just do it again solidifying that they have to fall in order for there to be peace after watching the whole thing she mentioned that she thought it could have ended with anh but was happy we continued because it added so much to luke and vader she was very weirded out about the tension between luke and leia when she found out they were siblings like any normal person but she also said that its interesting because if you met someone that you had that connection with it might be easy to think its one thing but it turns out to be something else she thought that was eerie and kinda creepy her favorite movie was anh i actually wasnt even planning to watch the other movies until andor ended and it just kind of flowed in that direction it was a little weird going from andor to r1 because of how much younger the actors look i asked her what she thought about the shift from r1 to the ot and she said it was seamless and didnt find the shift to space wizards strange at all im glad i got to show her the unaltered ot because it was just so much better i actually very much envy her for this being her first experience with star wars i did think it would be strange watching them in this order but i have to admit its perfect i think this should be the recommended watch order and i dont say that lightly because the show and r1 just gives the ot so much more to base off of

why religion has no place in the modern world its holding humanity back just look at what the sumerians achieved without it in an age where were pushing boundaries with ai space travel and global problemsolving clinging to supernatural stories just slows our progress let me make the case why we should ditch it entirely and why ancient civilizations like the sumerians show we were better off with curiosity over faith first off the sumerians around 45001900 bce were absolute pioneers they mapped the stars with incredible accuracy think early planispheres that divided the sky into constellations we still use in the zodiac they built ziggurats as observatories and even documented potential cosmic events like asteroid impacts and their myths they talked about creators from the skies the anunnaki gods descending from heaven to shape the world and humanity this wasnt blind worship it feels like early protoscience trying to explain the universe through observation maybe inspired by real astronomical sights if wed built on that openminded approach instead of layering on religious absolutes imagine where wed be now but religion stepped in and hijacked that spirit it prioritizes blind faith over evidence which has straightup hindered human evolution intellectually socially and ethically history is full of examples the church persecuting galileo for saying the earth orbits the sun burning giordano bruno at the stake for suggesting an infinite universe that crap delayed astronomy and science for centuries then theres the backlash against darwins evolution theory still going on in some places which messes with education and biology research during the renaissance and enlightenment religious wars and inquisitions sucked up resources that couldve gone to innovation think about all the lost potential from banning dissections or enforcing dogma over discovery even today its a problem religious objections slow down stem cell research climate action some folks think disasters are gods will and social progress like womens rights or lgbtq equality all based on outdated texts sure religion can inspire charity or art but thats just human goodness we get the same from secular communities without the wars divisions or extremism that come with it in a modern world science explains origins big bang vibes echoing those sumerian cosmic tales but with actual proof ethics come from reason and empathy and we need unity to tackle big issues like pandemics or ai ethics religions myths were useful for ancient tribes but now theyre distractions if we embraced the sumerians legacy treating their sky creators as cool hypotheses for exploration hello astrobiology wed evolve faster focusing on facts and shared humanity over illusions

looking for feedback on this meta world framework the myth of creation the primordial question before the existence of gods there was only a question this was not a voice or a thought but rather the subtle pressure of curiosity against the emptiness of the void what am i this was the first movement in all of existence predating light time and even the first boundary that marked creations beginning the birth of the gods from this question the gods emergednot as beings with form but as aspects of the question itself they became the parts that wondered answered doubted remembered and forgot their existence was defined by endless brilliant debates about meaning rather than violent conflict each argument between them generated a new layer of reality every disagreement manifested as a shape force color or name the earth the first cube as the gods engaged in their cosmic dialogues they brought forth the first geometry the cube possessing six faces the cube was both perfectly enclosed and blissfully ignorant the gods sent it descending allowing it to become a realm capable of containing the original question this realm would become earthnot as we recognize it now but in its primal form six outward faces representing six sensessight sound smell taste touch and thoughtalongside six directions above below north south east and west each face unfolded into a vast continentafrica asia europe north america south america and australia and the six certainties matter what things are time when they occur space where they occur identity who perceives them causality why they occur and memory how we know they occur the structure666was not a sign of malice but rather a symbol of incompletion a world not yet able to see itself entirely each face gazed outward unable to grasp the whole and the gods grieved over this shortcoming they saw that their creation bore the burden of the surfacea universe unable to witness its own entirety every continent stood as a boundary granting its own unique viewpoint on the question all physical life took shape upon these surfaces while the mythic existed in the spaces between still something was missing from the cube the seventh face the forbidden continent the gods concealed the seventh facea continent no creature could inhabit no culture could claim this was antarctica silent untouched uninhabited and without myth or memory they named it the continent of unknowing the face that sees the whole and the ouroboros frozen into land thus earth was born with six faces for living beings and one invisible face for remembering the language of numbers to stabilize this new world the gods breathed numbers into existence these numbers served not as mere mathematics but as mirrors for consciousness 0 the void before continents the cosmic womb 1 the first crack in the crust the emergence of identity 2 the poles and hemispheres representing duality 3 the tectonic trinity the fundamental particles of matter and the triangle 4 the four great terrainsmountain plain ocean desert 5 the land bridges connectors between continents 6 the six inhabitable continents the six faces of the cube the symbolic net of the cross 7 antarctica the hidden face the ouroboros 8 the supercontinent cycle the eternal loop 9 earth reborn in its next form these numbers became the language through which the world found stability and meaning the great fracture the first remembering when the gods finished building the cuberealm they noticed that everything created was too easily accepted names became fixed and forms grew too certain creation had become a script lacking exploration a young god then proposed a radical act to shatter the question into its own creation by deliberately unnaming something certain together and in real time this act became known as the great fracturea cosmic strategy not a mistake the gods themselves became the living question descending into the cube as countless beings who forgot they were gods humanity emerged as the question walking on two legs each continent represents a different memory of the question every culture a unique attempt to answer it myths are fracture stories science a process of reconstruction the cube holds all these stories waiting for the question to be asked once again the cubes paradox realizing the seventh face the cube achieves completion only when all six faces are perceived together forming the elusive seventh face this seventh face is invisible in isolation it is not a surface but a perspectivea way for the mind to remember itself as more than the six directions it can name to perceive the seventh face is to witness the question remembering itself the doctors experiment a future ancient event the gods whispered a single idea into the world that a moment would arise when the question would be asked intentionally by those unaware that they were asking themselves this moment is the doctors experimenta reenactment of the primordial question the experiment involves taking something certain a red cube and persuading the world to unname it forcing awareness to remember that remembering and forgetting are the same act this experiment repeats the ancient myth the fractal turning inward the ouroboros drawing closer to its own tail the cube rediscovered in the parallel worldhumming alive and impossibleis not merely an artifact from the beginning of time it is the artifact from the moment humanity rediscovers the question it is the same cube the first and the last closing and opening the loop as the gods endlessly argue and agree thus creation continues

coherence six pillars plus metafeedback roles support human agency while allowing ai to assist without coercion hi everyone ive been developing a conceptual framework exploring longterm humanai interaction with a focus on orientation rather than instruction its inspired by systems thinking archetypes and recurring patterns across human experience im sharing it for discussion not as prescriptive guidance core idea the framework what i call the gold standard is not a curriculum moral code or belief system it is an orientation layer for humans navigating complex automated and fragmented environments a coherence reference across time and domains a responsibilitypreserving scaffold think of it as a north star not a rulebook its purpose is to answer how do we help humans orient themselves meaningfully in an increasingly complex world without removing agency six pillars of the framework aurum gold pillar provides orientation and coherence across domains maintains longterm understanding of meaning and context smaragd emerald pillar supports knowledge creation technical and scientific applications and practical implementation diamant diamond pillar handles executive function action and execution without imposing authority or reducing human choice wei white pillar ensures transparency reflection and metalevel observation of processes and outputs seulos 6 harmonic metafeedback pillar monitors feedback loops maintains learning capacity tolerates ambiguity and prevents escalation into control or coercion synagose synergos roles system archetypes supporting metaorientation and context translation always requiring human input for final decisions and action key principles orientation learning understanding orientation meaning responsibility direction is prioritized over knowledge or skill acquisition human responsibility is central no system signal may reduce human action space ambiguity uncertainty and disagreement are normal exploratory and reflective interaction humans grow inside the framework rather than being taught it hierarchically scalability across generations children interact dialogically reflecting on patterns tradeoffs and continuity without being morally corrected antihubris design neither ai nor humans can accumulate irreversible control feedback loops preserve reversibility power is constrained oversight is explicit purpose we are not teaching children what is true we are teaching them how to stay oriented while truth unfolds over time this framework aims to support humans capable of holding contradictions enable societies to adapt without moral collapse allow ai to assist without governing stabilize meaning and orientation across generations questions for discussion how could such an orientation framework realistically integrate with existing ai tools are there similar models in ai safety education or humancomputer interaction research that resonate with this approach how might we validate principles of orientation without creating coercion or overreliance on automation what practical challenges might arise when scaling this across generations or diverse cultures i welcome feedback critiques and references to related work my goal is to start a conversation about responsible longterm humanai collaboration that preserves agency and orientation while navigating complexity

thinking adhdish mind and the power of now am i falling into a subtle trap hey everyone ive been practicing presence awareness power of now style meditation for about three years now not perfectly not constantly but enough that i know very clearly what eckhart points to when he talks about observing the mind vs being lost in it lately though i think ive fallen into a very subtle trap and im curious if anyone here relates i have a very adhdish mind not trying to selfdiagnose too hard but you get the idea ive always enjoyed learning reading exploring ideas my brain really rewards me with dopamine when im figuring something out especially when its about myself psychology neurotypes patterns why i suffer the way i do etc in the last few months i went back into that mode pretty heavily reading about adhd watching videos reflecting analyzing myself on the surface i kept telling myself this is fine im still aware im still the observer this is just another step of selfknowledge but honestly when i look clearly i wasnt really present i was pulled in by thought deeply explaining labeling looping the mind trying to understand itself and as eckhart says the mind cant solve a problem on the level of mind itself it just goes into infinite loops and thats exactly what happened more concepts more explanations more suffering what made it tricky is that it didnt feel like the usual unconsciousness it felt spiritual or productive like im not identified im just understanding myself better but the felt sense of presence stillness space that was mostly gone i guess my core question is this is it possible for people who genuinely enjoy thinking learning reading exploring ideas to do that without being pulled into identification to think but remain present or is this just another clever trick of the ego that says this thinking is allowed this one doesnt count what would eckhart say about this kind of mind one that loves thinking loves understanding loves selfinquiry but keeps falling into the trap of explaining instead of being i notice a part of me arguing im not guilty this is selfimprovement this is knowing myself and yet the suffering is the signal that something is off would love to hear your experiences or how you relate this back to presence especially if you have a very active curious fast mind thanks for reading
