spoilers the expanse a telltale game review id held off on getting the game for ages in the hope that theyd eventually release a physical version but the deluxe edition being dirt cheap in the christmas sale pushed me over the edge finally plus the devs just kindastopped after the game released so i figured a physical would never happen i had a lot of fun with it i enjoy the modern pointandclick style of the game so i had no trouble getting into it and the foundations were great all the returning characters except dawes were voice by their actual actors which was great and we got brian george back as arjun in the bonus episode the set design sound efffects props and music were fantastic slightly stylised characters aside you could go from the game into the show seemlessly i enjoyed the setup to the story a lot it was a typical action adventure story but the individual pieces really elevated it drummer was fantastic and i enjoyed the crew of the artemis a lot they all felt authentic to the setting and were fun companions to have along it also included some amazing additions to the lore getting to explore that abandoned mining asteroid from the early days of the belt was so cool it was fascinating and tragic to learn that abuse of the belters existed before there were any belters as we know them during the series it was a good call to take the typical crazy space cult and twist it into something deeper my gripes with the game are few firstly obviously that it never got a physical release id have loved to put it on my shelf next to the blurays holding out hope on osiris for that secondly that it was waaay too short i finished the game in just 7hrs thats not too bad for a game like this when you think about it but when i was playing it felt like i was blasting through it too fast and i took my time exploring for the logs and salvage thirdly most glaringly i hate hate hate that the macguffin was protomolecule its lazy writing that makes the universe feel small and is only there because the show did it and whats worse is that it never plays a part in the story it never breaks free and causes havoc or ends up being the sample used on ganymede or anything its just a grey cylinder thats blown up at the end and is only protomolecule because thats a thing fans would recognise and would allow them to seed way more easter eggs into the game it couldve been literally anything else and had the same impact on the story overall it was a fun adventure that takes place just prior to the start of the show aesthetically its almost flawless the characters were great and getting to play as drummer was great its no masterpiece but if you love the expanse and want a fun adventure more of the universe drummer and avasarala then absolutely pick it up when its on sale ps why was it called a telltale game i know during its release it was hyped up as the return of the studio but the credits for the game put deck nine front and centre in everything i didnt pay too much attention sure but it seemed like the word telltale didnt appear at all outside of the title my assumption is just that it was all marketing

2025 game recap intro its that time of year again and a time ive honestly really been looking forward to it seems i played far more than i remembered but it was an absolute blast reliving the memories and experiences i had and im happy to share them with yall because of the number of games ive tried to keep each review and overview focused on the major beats of what made it memorable but am more than happy to expand in the comments if you want a more indepth recap for context on average i play games about 2 to 3 hours per day this year ive broken my games down into their respective genres as best i could in some cases to allow users to jump to their gaming preferences ive also called out the highlights for this year those games that i thoroughly enjoyed had a very memorable experience with andor found very impactful never before played or completed and recommend to fans of the genre previously beaten and still recommend the experience a game recommended for nearly everyone to try regardless of genre likely my favorite from the genre this year its worth noting most of the games on this list were acquired through some kind of bundle that means my perspective is not skewed by any sort of buyers remorse considering i felt conformable with the price point and removed from any possible hype it also meant i was exposed to titles i may have never considered while i dont have high commendations for every game i did find something to enjoy in every title nbsp platformer super magbot super magbot is a 2d sidescrolling twinstick platformer that feels like the offspring of super meat boy and a hint of celeste it features some incredible mechanical pacing with a surprisingly fresh gimmick for platforming with the magneticbot using attract and repel to make their way through these bitesized levels this game felt amazing on a gamepad and hits a really nice flow youd see in the games that inspired it absolutely recommended to anyone who likes the genre pumpkin jack from what i can tell pumpkin jack is an adventure platformer made by a sole developer given that perspective its quite impressive what they put together it has a fairly great atmosphere and really sets that halloween sort of vibe and ambience unfortunately its not a bad game just a touch of a miss for me most levels feature some kind of donkey kong countryesque mine cart interlude and they last just a little too long even the games run time which is only about 4 to 5 hours feels like its on the cusp of overstaying that being said i still enjoyed it for what it was but know what youre getting into mario 64 i think ive played and completed mario 64 with my kids for the past three or so years and every time its still so enjoyable its so shocking to me that any developer could achieve the level of finesse and technical capability in movement in their first real foray into the 3d realm however mario 64 stands as a testament for incredibly nuanced movement tech that even outpaces many of its modern competition even if it does take a moment to acclimate donkey kong 64 donkey kong 64 is the first and somewhat infamous 3d entry in the donkey kong franchise while this game gets somewhat memed and deservedly so i still love it despite its flaws its a fair bit janky as many n64 games were but it has a ton of heart and features a collection of worlds and ambience thats hard to find elsewhere i think the most glaring issue is the lack of quality of life to assist in reducing collectathon tedium planet cube edge another platforming entry that takes inspiration from super meat boy and the end is nigh i found the game and its difficulty curve great and would love to recommend it were it not for getting softlocked in an enemy arena about 6 times in a row with no way to progress ultimately it was a dnf which is rather unfortunate cavern of dreams i absolutely adored this game you play as a little red dragon named fynn in search of your siblings its a throwback to retrostyle n64 platformer collectathons and absolutely nails the feeling its fairly comfy and casual offering a low barrier to entry with some surprisingly higher skill ceilings if you learn the movement and associated techs you can actually forgo most upgrades whats great is the game really respects your time only clocking in at about 410 hours depending on your completion preference between the atmosphere low stakes story and balance between casual and more able players the game is truly a hidden gem webbed webbed is a 2d physicsbased puzzle platformer where you play as a webslinging spider who shoots lasers this game is a touch goofy considering that last aspect but it absolutely feels amazing swinging around as a little spider with some great pixel art and music to boot i think my biggest gripes would be the tedium of some of the puzzles although watching a dung ball roll away from the top of the tree and seconds from its destination was both harrowing and comedic gold and the fixed zoom theres a few times where it would have been great to have a larger perspective especially as some web shots are blind still the game is fairly dense and straight to the point in its roughly 5 hour run time nbsp arpgdiablolike warhammer chaosbane the demographics for arpgs tend to fall between the veterans who absolutely thrive off the endgame or the casuals who are looking for an engaging story or world with some solid player progression i think the truth is there are others in the genre who achieve this much more handedly its not a particularly bad game but it feels like it would really only appeal to warhammer fans looking for a game with that coat of paint overall i did enjoy my time but its not a genre classic or particularly definitive nbsp deckbuilder roguebook roguebook is a roguelite deckbuilder where you battle in the book of lore of faeria using ink to explore the pages uncover treasures and take the fight to monsters it took me a second to appreciate the mechanics but the actual exploration mechanic is fairly novel and a welcome change from the branching paths popularized by slay the spire where the game truly shines and subsequently loses a bit of ground is in its difficulty modifiers the early modifiers are so unbelievably well done sometimes drastically altering strategies and approach the biggest letdown is that they werent cumulative and the latter difficulty modifiers were fairly run of the mill harder bosses which was essentially more damage less gold etc in the grand scheme it felt more like a missed opportunity than a real negative regardless the game comes as an easy recommendation nitro kid nitro kid is a retrofuturistic synthwave tactical deckbuilder you play as one of three characters each of which has a very different focus from one another progressing through arena after arena its very reminiscent of fights in tight spaces fits with great art direction some fitting music and some great tactics gameplay overall i enjoyed the game but for whatever reason it did not reach the same heights as fits for me aces and adventures this is a bit of an odd one as its a fantasybased roguelite deckbuilder with an emphasis on elements of poker its very niche and unique and thats what i love about it aces and adventures has an amazingly simple but effective presentation and really added to the whole experience in general i thought it had some surprisingly effective combat and strategic elements while balancing luck relatively well hexarchy hexarchy asks the question what if we made civilization a deckbuilder weirdly it works its a mashup id never thought id see but i applaud the uniqueness runs are significantly shorter than any comparable civ game and much more digestible however the downside is theres significantly less player investment and the variety in each game doesnt warrant the same kind of one more turn mentality civ holds i still enjoyed my time but think its a bit more niche sitting at the intersection of deckbuilder and 4x toads of the bayou toads of the bayou is a roguelike deckbuilder where you play as one of three characters trying to stop baron samedi this game is a bit confusing to me it has some pretty gorgeous pixel art and the actual strategy and gameplay are a bit like a deckbuilder version of into the breach however while that may sound utterly incredible the game was a bit less impressive than that partially the strategy from deckbuilding gets a bit in its own way especially because the variety of cards isnt broad enough theres also the resource earned during a run that doesnt feel like it meaningfully contributes since theres no kind of permanent progression or unlocks theres not anything wrong with that approach but theres just something about the game that didnt land quite the same as some of the other titans in the genre pyrene pyrene is a unique deckbuilder thats tough to even describe let me just start by saying i was not wowed by the screenshots or even the title screen but im so glad i gave it the chance i cannot begin to describe how much this game resonated with me you play as a character whose deck distributes on the world amongst other randomly distributed monsters and other miscellaneous items you move in a grid clearing cards as you try to clear the danger zone this is the core loop that takes place until you beat the boss of the biome while it might not sound engaging i highly encourage you check the game out as it does offer a demo the music is incredible the story is short but done well as it introduces mechanics and the strategy and mechanics of the different characters all feel unique and satisfying the only real downside which will come down to preference is a lack of native gamepad support deepest chamber resurrection deepest chamber resurrection is a roguelite deckbuilder where you control a party of three i love the presentation of the game the battles are set up like a firstperson dungeon crawler and this probably has one of the more unique takes ive seen on a deckbuilder where order and position of card playing in the players hand matters greatly each card can be boosted so long as a card is played next to it adding boost enhances the damage or utility of a card and matters immensely to winning battles while it has a lot to love im still currently split on whether its a game i can recommend theres little in the ways of defense and so it feels like a war of attrition not to mention i cant quite figure out if the game is balanced or not i change strategy every run which means each new difficulty could be the fault of a new archetype or a focus thats not actually viable regardless of my thoughts this game features a demo and you ought to check it out isle of swaps isle of swaps is a roguelike deckbuilder with a touch of creature collector a la the pokmon card game i actually played the tutorial and then set this game down for about a month before coming back because initially i was left perplexed and wanting im glad i took that time to give it a fair shake because its surprisingly unique with an incredible premise essentially its a card battler in a school yard where youre battling other tamers or trying to capture wild critters through about 24 total encounters the actual strategy can be surprisingly complex and the different aspects are unlike anything id seen from the genre its a very easy recommend but do note that it may take some acclimation from the player and doesnt have native gamepad support nbsp roguelite voidigo this game is incredible its basically a love letter to nuclear throne it has some fairly goofy guns incredible synergies is highly fastpaced and really emphasizes the bullet hell aspect for those who like it i got some similar feelings to when i played enter the gungeon and for any fans of nuclear throne look no further dreamscaper dreamscaper is a roguelite where you play as cassidy a woman who recently moved to the city of redhaven in an effort to escape the traumas of her past by day youll explore the city locales and talk with locals and by night youll delve into your dreams to take on your mental anguish what really sells the game for me is the whimsy of the weapons in your dreams and the very real slice of life kind of interactions with the residents its also got some great synergies built into the passive items decent meta progression and some killer and responsive combat easily one of my favorite roguelites ive played ziggurat 2 this year was absolutely packed with incredible roguelites for me so its a shame ziggurat 2 didnt take the top spot ziggurat 2 is a magicbased boomer shooter roguelike that improves on nearly every aspect of the first game enemy weapon and environment variety were all improved while maintaining the core gunplay which was already really enjoyable its an easy recommendation for roguelite and fps fans right and down and dice this is one of the best dicebased games ive played especially when i consider just how different the abilities and focus for each character are one thing i loved was how the final difficulty for each character was cumulative the only downside was the downtime due to animations which really added up when you considered each of six character had five difficulties to progress through overall its a great game but respect for player time could have been a bit improved astral ascent astral ascent is a sidescroller action roguelike where youre trying to escape from the garden this game feels like a marriage between dead cells fluid combat utterly gorgeous and themed bosses of hades greek gods replaced by the zodiacs and wizard of legends four ability customization and cooldown management allinall its a fantastic game where the biggest letdown comes at the procedurally generated levels feeling a bit samey even despite the changes in theme that said easy recommendation to anyone who enjoyed dead cells but liked the difficulty curve in hades with the heat customization space prison space prison is a turnbased roguelite game where you play as a convict attempting to escape the galaxys most brutal prison it has a great comicbookesque artstyle with some decently engaging tactical combat the biggest issue is the pacing its fairly appropriately challenging at the start with a somewhat oppressive midgame but once you overcome that hump it becomes laughably easy one of the aspects most fitting to the game is arguably one of the least enjoyable the crafting and contraband system you have a limited inventory and crafted items have extremely low durability its not the worst ive seen but grows tiresome by the end of the game madshot madshot is a lovecraftian sidescroller twinstick shooter roguelite the gameplay itself is actually relatively solid but is weighed down by a lack of polish where every won run i had to save quit to title screen because it went to black screen a lack of variety and item balancing issues i enjoyed my time but itd be hard to recommend over others in the genre deadlink deadlink is a cyberpunk roguelite fps where you play as the titular character deadlink in a simulation it has some great visuals snappy and responsive gameplay with exceptional movement and stellar music id liken its gameplay similar to something like doom eternal with how fastpaced and hectic it is coupled with your ability management arenabased fights and verticality that being said the biggest letdown is the overall variety in both locations and enemies youll quickly see everything the game has to offer i very much enjoyed my brief time with it and it did not overstay its welcome curse of the dead gods curse of the dead gods is an isometric action roguelike where you scour a long forgotten temple in search of riches and relics the gameplay is solid but i was fairly lukewarm on the game overall enemy variety is low much of the environments are shrouded and drowned out in darkness and while theres a ton of weapons their variety didnt really feel that meaningful to me once i nailed down the parry system i still really enjoyed the curse system and how it could drastically alter your playstyle for the run but overall this one was only fine for me source of madness source of madness is a sidescroller roguelite where you play as a new acolyte to a lovecraftian cult the visuals and world were somewhat reminiscent of noita without the gameplay to match the enemies are randomly generated masses of limbs which while fitting to the theme do not make for engaging fodder that mixed with a pendulum that swings between severely under or overpowered and you either end up with an absolute slog or a laughably easy run crypt of the necrodancer crypt of the necrodancer is a turnbased rhythm roguelike where you brave the depths of the crypt and its denizens to the beat of the music i downloaded it again to play with my kids this year and knocked out a few more character wins its one of my favorite games that i cant quite master despite that its an easy recommendation because of the great music and art and theres nothing else quite like it nbsp soulslike hellpoint hellpoint is a scifi soulslike that takes place on irid novo a derelict space station i was lukewarm on this game to start but most soulslikes take a minute to acclimate to and take in the setting and boy did i end up loving the setting the combat itself felt a bit floatyjanky in a similar manner to dark souls 2 still good but if you went from ds3 to ds2 for instance itd feel a touch uncanny that being said i ended up adoring the lore and notes youre exposed to and found the actual boss setpieces not the regular enemies disguised as minibosses to be interesting and enjoyable enotria the last song enotria is an italian soulslike that has the player taking part in a macabre grand play i recommend the game because its so gorgeous and unique but be warned it lacks polish with ai sometimes stopping mid fight elevators disappearing crashes and other possible issues that out of the way its probably one of the most intriguing worlds both in regards to its dark whimsical setting and its absolutely gorgeous environments couple that with some decently interesting bosses and some surprisingly robust combat and its easy to see the vision ultimately it falls well short of its full potential but it was dripping with ambition and i felt it my entire playthrough flintlock siege of dawn flintlock is a soulslite emphasis on the lite game where you play as nor vanek a sapper trying to repel the onslaught of the dead this game has a fairly middling opening and doesnt come into its own until the player gets a few upgrades however the actual gameplay feels fairly fluid with some solid movement and satisfying variety in combat abilities to weave into your battles the actual boss fights are interesting but limited to a handful of setpieces and not too difficult what i really enjoyed was the dialogue between our companion characters i think the categorization by the developer does the game a disservice but i found it surprisingly enjoyable sands of aura sands of aura is an open world soulslike that has you seeking salvation for a civilization at risk of dying the game starts out fine but doesnt truly shine until you have the opportunity to explore its rather unique setting i adored the travel in this game even though it was rather mindless from island to island still it was novel to fly through the sands and off dunes into the air the actual camera sits a bit oddly for my taste but i grew accustomed to it and found the combat fairly decent if not needing a touch of acclimation asterigos asterigos is a romangreek inspired soulslike where you play as hilda looking for your dad and his team who was sent to explore the city of aphes this is probably one of the easiest soulslikes ive played even on the hardest difficulty so challenge is not the main driver here truthfully its a wonderful and gorgeous world to explore with a fairly interesting story premise i enjoyed my time with it but its in a weird spot where its going to drive away nonsouls players and fail to impress souls fans i wouldnt call it a mid experience by any means but the weird crossroads it chose to sit at feels a bit alienating salt and sacrifice salt and sacrifice is the 2d sidescroller soulslike metroidvania following the someone cult favorite of salt and sanctuary much of this game is more of the same with a few exceptions areas are now connected by a singular hub a la demon souls and the actual method for reaching the fixed bosses means going through the equivalent of hunts from a monster hunter game im actually surprised to see it wasnt received positively as it felt like more salt and sacrifice which is actually why i didnt enjoy it as much i thought the first game was pretty good if not on the easy side with a fairly meaningless stat dump skill tree this game was essentially more of the same interesting worlds and enemies with decent combat but most bosses didnt take more than one or two tries at worst nbsp metroidvania withering rooms in truth im not sure it belongs here as withering rooms is a mishmash of genres blending mechanics from metroidvanias roguelites horror and soulslikes regardless its a game unlike any others and an easy recommendation the actual combat is a touch janky giving the impression that encounters are better worth avoiding however it really is so unique and memorable that i cant help but recommend it as i still often reminisce on my own experience gestalt steam and cinder gestalt features an incredible setting as steampunk doesnt have the same prevalence that straight fantasy and scifi do its a decent enough game but thats about it i still enjoyed the experience but it didnt have the same kind of impact something like grime hollow knight or blasphemous did the game is also fairly short coming in at between 4 and 6 hours or so afterimage afterimage is a metroidvania where you play as renee working to recover your lost memories the game and art style are absolutely stunning and is one of the biggest draws here the actual gameplay feels relatively tight and responsive with the usual ability upgrade tropes however the difficulty especially on bosses is somewhat disappointing i think i beat most bosses on the first try the game is also fairly expansive theres a lot to explore and unfortunately some of it just isnt that interesting i will give a shout to the platforming though it had a fair bit of challenge that i enjoyed nbsp tactics lost eidolons lost eidolons is a tactics game where you play as eden leading a team of your mercenary compatriots this game feels like the b movie to fire emblems blockbuster while that may sound like a criticism i found the game wonderfully endearing it faces typical tactics tropes where critical information is obscured from the player reinforcementsambush that would drastically alter your approach to a particular battle but also has some really enjoyable side characters its still a solid tactics game even if its a bit campy at times dream tactics dream tactics is a deckbuilder tactics game where you play as neru trying to save the dream world initially i was a bit nonplussed by this game as it felt fairly plain in presentation strategy and even enemy variety by the end though im glad i stuck with it it has some fairly decent humor and while the enemy variety is low in regards to aesthetics it actually does become somewhat funny and make sense within the context of the game what actually surprised me was how good the actual tactics aspect was compelling and interesting companion synergies with varied and unique itemization while it didnt have the strongest first impression it wrapped up by being one of my favorites for the year and an easy recommendation druidstone secret of the menhir forest druidstone secret of the menhir forest is the followup game from the studio who delivered the highly acclaimed grimrock games and a somewhat divisive departure from the dungeon crawling classics while i love grimrock i have no issues with a developer experimenting and i think they made a rather competent tactics game the biggest issue for me was the rather heavy handed use of humor and sarcasm which diminished the tone of the story i think the mission structure enemy reinforcements and resource management all made ambushes or objective changes all the more jarring despite it being the norm for the genre its tough because i genuinely liked the game but am not fully sure whether to recommend it for those reasons subterrain mines of titan subterrain mines of titan is a tactics scifi rpg where you play as the survivor of a colony that went dark this game starts off on a strong note intriguing setting a broad spread of skills usagebased skill gains and a decently robust customization of difficulty however the game does falter a bit along the way subterrain mines of titan is a relatively linear dungeon crawler that introduces a fair bit of tedium in its crafting system even the actual fighting grows tiresome as the game goes on because of how the infection mechanic works i actually toned down crafting and infection based on reviews before starting and even then it was on the cusp of irritating its rather unfortunate as theres a lot to like here and i did enjoy my time but fair warning that it misses the mark towards endgame desperados 3 since i go into most games with very little information i had not realized this was an isometric realtime with pause stealth game typically stealth is not one of my favorite genres but desperados 3 was an absolute blast it had a great introduction of abilities mechanics and difficulty pacing and there was nothing quite as satisfying as a plan coming to fruition the game encourages a trial and error approach which i found grating after a point but that says less about the game and more about me taking the time to analyze the situations i will likely not play another game like this knowing what it is now but i can easily recommend it not being a fan of the genre nbsp casual paleo pines paleo pines is a cozy dinosaur ranching and farming game you move to the valley with your parasaurolophus lucky where you join a local community in search of others of his kind the game is incredibly cute but relatively shallow in its mechanics most of the appeal is exploration based and comes from discovering and finding new dinos actually managing your ranch and relationships is fine but overall others in the genre have done the other cozy aspects better still the dinosaur angle is surprisingly underutilized in games which makes the game desirable even despite its flaws in the end i did dnf because of a glitch preventing me from getting a necessary item to progress smushi come home smushi come home is a lowstakes adventure platformer where you play as a mushroom separated from your family its incredibly wholesome and meshes some reasonable collectathon mechanics with some retrostyle graphics the game is incredibly cute familyfriendly and extremely respectful of your time total playtime clocks in at around 4 to 6 hours depending on your level of exploration i highly recommend it to nearly everyone looking for a relatively wholesome escape katamari damacy katamari damacy has you play as the prince helping to restore celestial bodies for the king of all cosmos by rolling objects from various locales onto your sticky ball i remember when katamari first released when i was younger and i scoffed at the concept fully confident like only a child could be that it was not for me fast forward about 20 years and i realized just how much i missed by being so closeminded i was fortunate enough to still be able to experience this bizarre game but i highly recommend everyone does at some point its so wonderfully weird from its art direction it objectives and even its music but it comes together in an unforgettable experience youre unlikely to have anywhere else nbsp adventure zelda ocarina of time whats to say this game is an absolute classic and for good reason despite the dated graphics it still looks great today because of the phenomenal art direction its a timeless classic with some at times obtuse guidance and it only gets more enjoyable as i dip my toes into randomizers and some of the games technical glitches if youve never played it its at least worth seeing part of the legacy from where modern zelda evolved cryptmaster very unique game that blends dungeon crawling with a typing game make your way towards the land of the living as a newly resurrected party of four the game features an ability discovery system that unlocks letter by letter through different combat encounters given the context of each characters archetype and personality it can be fun to try and rack your brain for words fitting the length and few letters revealed it also has a very dry sense of humor which i very much enjoyed black skylands black skylands is a top down adventure game where you play as eva an airship captain defending your home from the falcons and swarm i think the idea is better than its execution you spend a lot of time on land for being an airship captain and i think the focus on both means neither is particularly great its still an enjoyable experience but is a bit more mindless than id have preferred falconeer falconeer is a dogfighter aerial combat game where you pilot giant falcons created by a solo developer its an impressive display and features a surprisingly robust world with some interesting politics and faction rivalry i think the world is one of the standout aspects here which i think says more about the actual combat than not its certainly not bad but i think it lacks a level of finesse id like to personally see in responsiveness and controllability for the birds that being said it could easily have been my own skill and not a fault of the game regardless i laud the level of ambition in the game and the rather unique premise and think its at least worth consideration edge of sanity a survival game similar in vein to this war of mine with a lovecraftian theme i enjoyed this one at the start as i found the slow reveal of what transpired enjoyable and the mechanics themselves were competent enough im a sucker for lovecraft and so i very much enjoyed the otherworldly horrors i encountered that is up until the last few missions in the game those missions became a trial and error kind of approach where one wrong step resulted in instant death unfortunately while it may be thematically apt i did not find it enjoyable and ultimately dnfed this war of mine this war of mine is a cult classic survival adventure game where you manage a group of individuals trying to survive in a war ravaged city i think its important to note that i lovingly refer to this game as a depression simulator this game has some amazing commentary on the impacts of war especially on civilians which leads to some rather somber moments its also a mechanically light game theres not a ton of systems but what it does implement it does well and it all feels cohesive and tight overall this is an incredible game if youre in a great spot mentally or are particularly resilient and i highly recommend it because theres not much like it nexomon extinction nexomon extinction is a creature collector game much like pokmon and the direct sequel to nexomon most creature collectors live or die by their character designs and i think nexomon extinction absolutely nails it the game also has some decent music though it is by multiple artists and you can really tell by the lack of cohesion the story itself is actually serviceable and features a dry comic relief fourthwall breaking character that actually got a chuckle from me multiple times i think the game has its pros and cons when compared to mainline pokmon with some enhancements in quality of life in some areas while others are missing overall its a great creature collector if youre in the mood for one but doesnt do a lot to shake up the genre nbsp rpg baldurs gate 3 baldurs gate 3 is the critically acclaimed rpg from larian studios where you play as either one of the main companions or elect to customize your own the game is much simpler than an owlcat pathfinder game in regards to the actual character progression and customization which is exactly why i think its a great game for people who do not typically enjoy the genre couple this with some great companions fantastic art direction and visuals and a highly reactive world and its an incredible experience the only real downside seems to be the consensus that the overall quality degrades from act to act but thats somewhat expected when you consider the amount of threads that have to resolve from all the player choices pathfinder wrath of the righteous pathfinder wotr is another crpg style game based on you guessed it the pathfinder tabletop game wotr is the motorcycle to baldurs gate 3s bicycle in terms of complexity featuring a system so robust you can look like the charlie and the red string corkboard meme from always sunny it has an amazing setting with some decent characters and the customization is unlike anything ive seen for both better and worse it can be absolutely overwhelming if not outright prohibitive to interested but uninitiated players on the other side it allows for some fairly varied builds i ran a bombardier alchemist for most of the game however the downside is while it was cool and very nice from a specialization standpoint it had minimal viability in the early or late game partially thats on me for not completely minmaxing but the game does have a fairly steep increase in difficulty towards the end though to be fair nongimmick builds can handle it overall its still easily one of my favorites and an easy recommend to anyone who likes crunchy rpgs atom rpg atom rpg is an isometric turnbased rpg that is very clearly inspired by early fallout i enjoyed this one and feel like its a worthy entry for any who find themselves nostalgic or interested in those style of games although playing as a dummy brute was better in theory than in practice actual interactions were fine but combat very clearly did not anticipate a solely melee focused character and i found it more challenging than it had any right to be partially my fault for sticking to the rp of my rpg but i did expect the game to account for it somewhat my biggest gripe was time spent traveling on the overworld was mind numbingly slow there was a stat to invest in to alleviate but again going back to the rp of an rpg i didnt want to metagame to reduce tedium still despite my grumbling i love a good postapocalyptic setting and this game does scratch the itch two worlds two two worlds two feels like a kind of time capsule back to the mid2000s which is pretty telling since it came out in 2010 where the protagonist was a sarcastic hardass with little else to show for their personality the game was fairly ambitious with a decently sized open world plenty of mechanics and systems and likely one of the more unique magic systems it had a fairly jank combat system and would have felt right at home with the gothic games had it not been so bland unfortunately the game is relatively milquetoast as its a cobbled collection of systems that dont feel cohesive and you can see a steady narrowing of scope as the game meanders towards its end still i actually enjoyed it but in a turnyourbrainoff sort of way greedfall greedfall is a fantasy rpg where you play as the legate to an alliance colonizing an island greedfall has some fairly nice atmosphere that really bring about that fall mood think skyrim outside of riften that however is where the game stops shining its not a bad game just middling where it has a lot of foundations to be more than that which is a bit unfortunate still the actual commentary on colonization as a concept isnt too often explored as a primary theme and so it was unique from that aspect nbsp fpsshooter wrath aeon of ruin wrath aeon of ruin is a boomer shooter the difference between most boomer shooters comes back to level design enemy variety arsenal and secret hunting overall the game was fine in all of these aspects but not particularly definitive i enjoyed my time with it but wouldnt recommend it unless youve made your way through some of the other genre leaders stalker clear sky stalker clear sky the prequel to shadow of chernobyl is an fps rpg where you play as scar this game is easily the weakest of the original trilogy with a healthy amount of bugs it quite possibly had the largest scope of the trilogy in regards to its ambition and mechanics which makes the subsequent shallowness of its depth rather unfortunate the faction and subsequent territory battle system was lackluster at best and gave a very superficial appearance of a living world the overall controls and mechanics were largely the same otherwise which meant you still got an enjoyable experience elsewhere but its easily the weakest in the trilogy however its still a stalker game which means it has some solid gunplay incredible environments and an oppressive world youre unlikely to find in many other games stalker call of pripyat stalker call of pripyat is the final entry in the original trilogy and easily the one i enjoyed most it maintains many of the mechanics from clear sky with more apparent side quests and a new map to explore stalker shadow of chernobyl shadow of chernobyl was the stalker developed but the second chronologically in the trilogy the mechanics are notably different especially around the artifacts which can sometimes feel like weeds with their availability metro 2033 metro 2033 is the antithesis to stalkers open world gameplay featuring a largely claustrophobic linear experience whereas most characters in stalker are voluntarily exploring the radioactive anomalous chernobyl zone the russian citizens of metro 2033 are facing the fallout of nuclear war this shift in narrative is often explored with an emphasis on reflecting the daily struggles the people of the metro face i absolutely adore the world of metro and the games presentation as i think the restriction in exploration helps guide the narrative and atmosphere as odd as it sounds theres something surprisingly cozy to me about the tunnels in which the people sought refuge its hard to cover the entirety of what makes the metro franchise great in so brief a summary but just know you ought to consider playing it for a memorable experience

settlements bases and reflections good morning adventurers im over 300 hours into this game and the more time passes the more i love it to be honest but i have a thought and i was wondering if others like me had the same idea overall base building is mostly about crafting elements found on planets but bases as beautiful and elaborate as they can be are empty theyre not alive and this always leaves a bad taste in my mouth settlements on the other hand are about managing events and the characters that populate them but theyre detached from the concept of base creation you take a settlement as you find it and you can do very little about its aesthetics over time ive combined bases and settlements together trying to unite the two but the end result didnt thrill me my idea is that the bases could become places that could be transformed into actual settlements a bit like in fallout 4 where the settlement you create is populated and needs to be taken care of do you think this would be an ideal update for the game i think so i love creating bases and creating homes and spaces to my liking and if these places could become inhabited and we could become like the mayor of the settlement it would be fantastic managing the dynamics of the settlements but being the architects of everything ourselves economy social life defense and the provision of essential goods for living what do you say we organize a huge petition to send to the developers lol but honestly even though i think its unlikely theyll listen to us it would be fantastic as a management tool to follow that said happy exploring and safe travels everyone

trip report 9 days in late december hi everyone i am at the airport with a long layover and just coming down from the postjapan high so i thought id put together a trip report to help gather my thoughts this was my first trip to japan and i was traveling solo overview 10 days9 nights nara kyoto kanazawa oshino im a history buff whos not really a fan of big cities so i decided to mostly focus on kyoto kyoto was surprisingly empty i was bracing myself for crazy crowds but most of the places i went had only a few people there was never more than one person in front of me in line for tickets and i was often the only customer in restaurants though i tend to eat earlier around 530 it was so calm and peaceful that i really regret not staying for a few extra nights i didnt plan my route very well and traveling from kanazawa to oshino ended up being slow and convoluted however riding the train was a great experience in itself the views are interesting and watching the shinkansen roar into the station was an unexpected highlight i hated the expressway busit was significantly delayed by traffic and very cramped there was so much condensation from people breathing that it was impossible to see the view if price is not a concern definitely take the train instead of the bus even if the bus route looks shorter on google maps beginner tip i found that google maps frequently underestimated the time needed to transfer especially with luggage something to keep in mind if youre trying to connect to a train that doesnt run that frequently nara 1 night hotel new wakasa i highly highly recommend this ryokan its a short walk to nara park and there is a gorgeous openair private bath on the roof that you can book i snagged the 5pm slot and watching the sun set over nara from a tub was magical sleeping on a futon on tatami was way more comfortable and fun than i anticipated the food was tasty but not exceptional overall impression maybe it was because it was my first stop but i loved nara so so much a lot of people recommend nara as a day trip but im glad that i stayed the night and even wish that i could have stayed an extra day as it gave me a lot more time to explore different corners of the park favorite sight todaiji temple this was my favorite temple in japan the scale is grandiose and the stark coloring combined with intricate wood architecture and sheer size makes it feel like it bears down on you with the weight of history hot take the deer are overrated honestly it was weird seeing animals that are not entirely wild yet not domesticated they did not look that healthy and it was a bit smelly where they congregated kyoto 4 nights hotel the thousand kyoto this is a beautiful new hotel right next to kyoto station its very artsy with an exquisitely designed aesthetic but the sound and light insulation were not great and the bathroom smelled of mold it was very convenient to be next to the train station though overall impression i absolutely fell in love with kyoto the temples shrines and gardens are so peaceful and beautiful and the fact that it was much emptier than expected made things perfect favorite sights shorenin temple this was my favorite temple in kyoto there are several tatami rooms where you can sit and look at the garden i just sat there and basked in the sunlight for an hour and a half it was so peaceful that it felt like time was flowing differently there ginkakuji i went about 45 minutes before closing and it was mostly empty this felt like the most aesthetically balanced temple to me with a beautiful mix of green gardens raked sand and simple wooden architecture goeido hall the scale of this place is really grand also im a simple person and it just makes me happy to be able to take off my shoes and walk on tatami nijo castle this was more crowded than the other places but it was quite interesting to visit something that wasnt a temple and see how architectural elements translated and changed this might be a good place to get a guide if youre inclined i eavesdropped on some of the tours and the stories about different shoguns were quite spicy it was lovely to see all the tourists wearing kimonoreally adds to the atmosphere day trip himeji wow himeji castle is one of the most breathtaking buildings i have ever seen it was also surprisingly empty when i arrived around 9 am on a monday theres not much on the inside but i enjoyed learning about princess sen from the exhibits in the long hall hot take biovortex is overrated well maybe not overrated but definitely not for me i found it too crowded and disorienting you spend several hours walking through dimly lit spaces with constantly changing projected colors flashing lights the press and heat of people and mirrors on every surface i do appreciate how much effort went into conceptualizing the exhibitsthe analogy between soap bubbles and an inverted lipid membrane in the soap sculpture exhibit was interesting i can definitely see why some people love this but for me it was too much kanazawa 2 nights hotel hyatt centric kanazawa nothing to complain of nice western chain hotel convenient location near the train station overall impression i was a little underwhelmed by kanazawa in hindsight i should have stayed a few extra days in kyoto instead of going there the sights seemed small and simplistic and the samurai houses felt very touristy however my impression was strongly shaped by the fact that there was a big snowstorm while i was there and being outside was miserable the city does not shovel the sidewalks at all of all the places i went only higashi chaya had any snow removal and this was done by spraying water to melt the snow resulting in an icy slushy mess im sure i would have liked kanazawa better if i had packed waterproof boots lesson learned media i did enjoy staying in my hotel room watching dousuru ieyasu during the worst of the storm its a cheesy surprisingly funny and moving if historically dubious biopic of tokugawa ieyasu restaurant rec haku kanazawa cuisine this was one of the best meals i had in japan its a newly opened omakase restaurant rather unexpectedly located in a mall food court the menu is amazing and the price is very reasonable for omakase 3600 jpy the restaurant only opened two weeks ago and the chefs are very friendly and chatty oshino hakkai 2 nights hotel konohanakan this is a new modernstyle ryokan with only 5 guest rooms and i highly highly recommend it the suites are huge larger than most apartments in new york and elegantly furnished and every room has a private openair onsen my room also had a fantastic view of mt fuji the kaiseki is delicious and the staff are super warm and kind overall impressions ive seen so many pictures of mt fuji that i was worried it might be a bit of a let down in person its not the mountain feels gigantic and incredibly close it visually dominates the entire skyline and is just aweinspiring the old town of oshino hakkai itself is an embarrassing tourist trap its the only place in japan where i went and literally thought what this is it its tiny consisting of a few old building and tiny springfed ponds kawaguchiko was beautiful but it was a weird mix of very crowded with a long line for the ropeway and other popular viewing sites and shut down the weather was good when i was there so there were amazing views of mt fuji but in december the sun is coming from the direction of the mountain so photos are backlit and i wished that i had brought sunglasses thanks for indulging me in this bit of retrospective navelgazing hopefully it doesnt break any rules i cant wait until i can go back
